item.title: Every English Ballon d’Or winner in history
item.description: Every English Ballon d’Or winner in history Harry Kane is among the favourites to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, with the England captain hoping to become the next Englishman to claim football’s most prestigious individual prize. Only four English players have won the award since its introduction in 1956, with Kevin Keegan the only one to lift the trophy twice. From Stanley Matthews making history as the inaugural winner to Michael Owen ’s memorable triumph in 2001, we look back at the English players who have been crowned the best in the world. Stanley Matthews (1956) Stanley Matthews was the first-ever recipient of the Ballon d'Or after winning the 1956 award. Matthews won the award at the age of 41, beating Real Madrid icons Alfredo Di Stefano and Raymond Kopa in the vote. The former Blackpool winger had earlier become the first winner of the FWA Footballer of the Year award in 1948. Bobby Charlton (1966) Bobby Charlton was crowned winner of the Ballon d'Or following his role in England's 1966 World Cup triumph on home soil. The Manchester United midfielder was England's joint-leading scorer at the tournament (3) and netted twice in the semi-final win over Portugal. Charlton was one of three Manchester United players to win the Ballon d'Or in just five seasons, as Denis Law (1964) and George Best (1968) also won the award. Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) Kevin Keegan remains the only Englishman to have won the Ballon d'Or twice. The forward earned back-to-back Ballon d'Or accolades in the 1970s, having cemented a reputation as one of the world's best after helping Liverpool to league and European Cup success in 1977. That summer saw Keegan sign for Hamburg for a British record fee of £500,000. He scored 12 times in his debut season to earn his first Ballon d'Or crown, before winning a second straight award after leading Hamburg to Bundesliga success in 1978/79. Michael Owen (2001) Michael Owen ended a 23-year wait for an English Ballon d'Or winner in 2001. Owen scored 24 goals in 46 games as Liverpool won a UEFA Cup, League Cup and FA Cup treble, with the forward netting both goals in the latter final win over Arsenal. Owen was also on target as Liverpool beat Deportivo Alaves 5-4 in a thrilling UEFA Cup decider, while a hat-trick for England helped the Three Lions thrash Germany 5-1 in World Cup qualification. At just 22 years and four days, Owen remains the second-youngest winner of the Ballon d'Or , behind only Ronaldo Nazario. Harry Kane (2026) Harry Kane became England's fifth Ballon d'Or winner after beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the 2026 award. With the 70-year anniversary celebrations held in London, Kane was a fitting winner of football's most prestigious individual accolade. Kane scored 73 goals for club and country in 2025/26, winning a German treble and helping England to third place at the 2026 World Cup.

item.title: NASCAR Fans Have Had Enough of Bubba Wallace at Talladega; Is He Becoming a Wreck Magnet?
item.description: Photo by: Bob Goshert Bubba Wallace cannot seem to escape the Talladega wreck conversation. Every time NASCAR heads to a superspeedway, Wallace seems to find himself at the center of another debate. Sometimes he is the victim. Sometimes he is part of the chain reaction. And sometimes, fans believe he should have known better. The latest Talladega race has only added fuel to that fire. Wallace and Ryan Blaney made contact during Sunday’s YellaWood 500, contributing to a major incident that swept up championship contenders. With the NASCAR title fight tightening, the consequences were enormous. But here is the question that keeps following Wallace: Is he simply an aggressive driver caught in superspeedway chaos, or does he deserve more blame for the wrecks he gets involved in? Why Does Bubba Wallace Keep Ending Up in These Conversations? Talladega is a different animal. Drivers run inches apart at nearly 200 mph, relying on drafting partners and perfectly timed pushes. One bad bump can send a car sideways and collect half the field before anyone has time to react. That makes it unfair to blame one driver automatically whenever a wreck happens. Still, Wallace has become one of the sport’s most polarizing figures, and incidents involving him tend to generate an outsized reaction. His aggressive style, high profile and history of superspeedway controversy make him an easy target for critics. That does not mean every criticism is justified. It does mean he rarely gets the luxury of an incident fading quietly into the background. Wallace has shown he can compete at the front on these tracks. But running near the front also puts him in position to influence how the biggest moments unfold. The question is whether his approach creates more opportunities to win or more opportunities to go home early. Is Wallace Racing Too Aggressively? Superspeedway racing requires aggression. Drivers who refuse to make moves can get trapped in the pack, lose track position and watch their chances disappear. But there is a difference between making a bold move and putting yourself in a position where one mistake destroys multiple cars. Wallace’s critics believe he sometimes crosses that line. His defenders argue that drivers cannot control every push, every lane change or every reaction from the cars around them. Both arguments have merit. The bigger problem is that NASCAR’s current superspeedway package often leaves very little room for error. A driver can make what looks like a routine move, only for the car ahead to become unstable and trigger a massive crash. That is exactly why the footage matters. His aggressive style, high profile and history of superspeedway controversy make him an easy target for critics. That does not mean every criticism is justified. It does mean he rarely gets the luxury of an incident fading quietly into the background. Wallace has shown he can compete at the front on these tracks. But running near the front also puts him in position to influence how the biggest moments unfold. The question is whether his approach creates more opportunities to win or more opportunities to go home early. Is Wallace Racing Too Aggressively? Superspeedway racing requires aggression. Drivers who refuse to make moves can get trapped in the pack, lose track position and watch their chances disappear. But there is a difference between making a bold move and putting yourself in a position where one mistake destroys multiple cars. Wallace’s critics believe he sometimes crosses that line. His defenders argue that drivers cannot control every push, every lane change or every reaction from the cars around them. Both arguments have merit. The bigger problem is that NASCAR’s current superspeedway package often leaves very little room for error. A driver can make what looks like a routine move, only for the car ahead to become unstable and trigger a massive crash. That is exactly why the footage matters. Fans should judge what actually happened instead of deciding who is guilty based on reputation alone. NASCAR Fans Have a Verdict to Deliver Wallace is not the first driver to become a lightning rod for criticism, and he certainly will not be the last. But he is one of the drivers who can dominate the conversation even when the wreck involves several competitors. That comes with being a recognizable name in a sport where every major incident gets replayed from a dozen angles. So let’s settle the debate. Is Bubba Wallace unfairly blamed because fans already dislike him, or does he need to take more responsibility for the chaos surrounding him at Talladega? And be honest: if another driver made the exact same move, would you judge it differently? NASCAR fans have strong opinions about Wallace. Now is the time to explain them.

item.title: FC Isle of Man launches women's football team
item.description: The new team will play six friendly matches before aiming to join a league next season. [FC Isle of Man] FC Isle of Man is launching a women's football team, with open training and trial sessions due to start next month. The club will hold the sessions at Colby AFC on Tuesday 10 November from 20:00 to 21:30. The team plans to play six friendly matches to begin with, before a possible move into league football subject to approval. Chairman David Pope said it was something the club "has wanted to achieve for some time". Pope said the club wanted to give young players the chance to compete at the highest level possible "without feeling they have to leave the Isle of Man". "Jersey and Guernsey are continually developing their sporting opportunities and there is no reason why the Isle of Man should not have similar ambitions," he said. He stressed the new team was not intended to take players away from existing clubs. "Our aim is not to detract from or adversely affect the local game, but to enhance it," he said. The team will be managed by Donna Harrison, supported by Sarah Wignall and Bex Corkish, with Luke Stewart and Ruairi Mooney as coaches. Pope said the club wanted women who love football, or who wanted to get back into the sport, to feel welcome. "This is their opportunity to be part of something from the very beginning," he said. Training will take place every Tuesday at Colby AFC, and the club is also looking for local businesses to sponsor the team. Read more stories from the Isle of Man on the BBC, watch BBC North West Tonight on BBC iPlayer and follow BBC Isle of Man on Facebook and X . New location for summer festival of football

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Heat off to worst start in 19 years
item.description: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Heat off to worst start in 19 years appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat entered the 2026-27 season with championship aspirations after acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster offseason trade. While those aspirations are very much alive and the Heat have time to turn things around, Miami is off to a very inopportune start to their season. Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat lost their fourth consecutive game to start the season, the latest a home contest against the Dallas Mavericks. Miami opened up the season with a 131-106 loss against the Minnesota Timberwolves, one of their three home losses to start the season. This is the first time that Miami has started 0-4 since the 2007-08 season and just the third time in franchise history. It’s also the first time in Antetokounmpo’s career that he’s lost four straight games to start a season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat have started the 2026-27 season with an 0-4 record. It's the first time they've started 0-4 since the 2007-08 season. pic.twitter.com/ORftYyIBqN — Tomer Azarly (@TomerAzarly) October 27, 2026 Giannis Antetokounmpo has been doing his part to start the year, averaging 28.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, 5.0 assists, and 1.0 steal per game while shooting 55.7 percent from the field in 31.6 minutes of play. The biggest question marks currently center around Bam Adebayo , who has not looked like himself as he and the Heat figure out how to play with their new teammates. In four games, Adebayo is averaging 11.8 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 2.0 steals, but is shooting just 40 percent from the field and 16.7 percent from three. The schedule doesn’t get any easier for Miami moving forward, with the Atlanta Hawks, Indiana Pacers, and Los Angeles Lakers as the next three opponents. Related: Heat legend Dwyane Wade shuts down unretirement talks with hilarious dunk story Related: Giannis Antetokounmpo needed just 3 quarters to pull off first triple-double with Heat

item.title: Whitwell reveals who will be in charge of Man Utd’s training session on Tuesday morning
item.description: Whitwell reveals who will be in charge of Man Utd’s training session on Tuesday morning Against all odds, Monday ended with Michael Carrick maintaining his post as Manchester United’s first-team head coach. Despite the team’s abysmal 0-3 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday, the Old Trafford faithful showered the 45-year-old with love and support, instead venting their frustration on the players, directors, and club owners. The consensus at the time was that Carrick would be made the scapegoat , with a Monday morning sacking looking inevitable. Michael Carrick continues to act as Man Utd coach (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) While the team was given the day off, it was still an eventful Monday at Carrington. CEO Omar Berrada, Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and Head of Recruitment Christopher Vivell all arrived in the morning and spent the bulk of the day congregating. Carrick, who wasn’t part of the discussion, arrived at the training facility in the afternoon to watch a friendly between Man Utd’s under-21 side and Hull City’s. The head coach and the club officials left afterwards, while no decision was communicated by the club, keeping the fans guessing. According to The Athletic’s MUFC correspondent Laurie Whitwell , Carrick is expected to take charge of the first team’s training session on Tuesday morning. In other words, the Wallsend native will continue to perform his duties as per normal, unless the management decides to change the narrative by officially relieving him of his duties. Will Carrick be charge of Man United’s game against Chelsea? (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) On Sunday evening, Carrick staying at the helm until the next game was almost unthinkable. After all, United are in desperate need of a reaction after slipping to a shocking 16th place in the Premier League table and failing to win a game in their last eight across all competitions. Carrick, who publicly locked horns with MUFC captain Bruno Fernandes after the Como defeat, has looked like he lost the plot a long time ago. And yet, his chances of making the weekend trip to West London are increasing with every passing hour. Perhaps the hierarchy is simply making the required arrangements before showing the former midfielder the door. But at this stage, no scenario can be completely dismissed. Eddie Howe is considered the big favourite to replace the under-fire manager, with Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as alternative options. item.title: Celtics’ Payton Pritchard gives Mike Conley Jr. ultimate veteran praise
item.description: Paul Rutherford-USA TODAY Sports Celtics’ Payton Pritchard gives Mike Conley Jr. ultimate veteran praise appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Payton Pritchard has played alongside plenty of talented teammates with the Boston Celtics , but Mike Conley Jr. has quickly earned a special place in his eyes. After powering Boston to a 134-99 rout of the Chicago Bulls on Monday night at TD Garden , Pritchard went out of his way to praise the 20-year veteran, who saw some late action in his home debut with the Celtics. “Just an unbelievable person. Obviously still in unbelievable shape for his age,” Pritchard said, via Zack Cox of Boston.com . “I was telling him (after) one of the back taps he had, I’m like, ‘You look like a DB still.’ Like, he’s just a freak.” Pritchard made it clear that Conley’s value goes well beyond what he does on the court. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “But just such a good vet to be around and somebody I’m always pulling knowledge from him,” Pritchard said. “Just his career has been unbelievable. So for me to have somebody like that in my corner, it’s big.” Conley signed a one-year deal with Boston in July , making him just the 14th player in NBA history to reach 20 seasons. The former Ohio State standout has built quite a resume along the way, earning an All-Star nod in 2021, an All-Defensive selection in 2013 and four NBA Sportsmanship Awards. He spent last season with the Minnesota Timberwolves, who traded him at the deadline before bringing him back on a minimum contract for the rest of the year. Pritchard, meanwhile, was the star of the show against Chicago. He scored a game-high 28 points on 10-of-16 shooting, including a scorching third quarter in which he poured in 19 points and went a perfect 5-of-5 from 3-point range. His barrage helped Boston take a 30-point lead into the fourth. Jayson Tatum added 23 points, seven rebounds and six assists, while Paul George chipped in 16 points. The lopsided score allowed the Celtics to rest their starters early, giving Conley and rookie Chris Cenac Jr. a chance to get on the floor . Cenac made his NBA debut and scored his first career points. Norman Powell led Chicago with 20 points. The win improved Boston to 2-1 on the season. The Celtics will not have long to celebrate, as they host the Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night to wrap up a back-to-back. Related: 76ers news: Why Lou Williams loves Jaylen Brown’s Jayson Tatum ‘beef comments Related: Celtics’ Payton Pritchard addresses slow start after 28-point night vs. Bulls

item.title: “Unserious League” “This Is Ridiculous”: Cathy Engelbert Once Again Faces WNBA Fans’ Wrath As Bizarre Issue Could Affect Dream vs Valkyries Game 6
item.description: Angel Reese and Gabby Williams in Practice Ahead of the WNBA Finals © WNBA/X Game 6 between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries is scheduled for Thursday at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. The game has been moved from the Dream’s regular venue, Gateway Center Arena, which seats 3,500, to the Atlanta Hawks’ 17,000-seat home. However, the venue change might be a big logistical issue. Game 6 of the WNBA finals is scheduled to start at 12:30 p.m. ET. However, the Atlanta Hawks also have a game on Thursday at 7:00 p.m. ET. Sportswriter Ramona Shelburne pinpointed how the Hawks game could affect celebrations if a WNBA champion emerges after Game 6. Fans were shocked when they realized it and held Cathy Engelbert accountable. “Unserious league,” one fan said . “This is ridiculous,” one fan said . The WNBA Commissioner has faced a lot of backlash this season. As she departs in December, the WNBA Finals have also drawn criticism of her leadership. Ramona Shelburne shares what would happen in a bizarre scenario Shelburne said winners’ celebrations could be cut short because of the Hawks game. “That celebration may not actually be on that court. I’ve heard there are discussions about whether there’s enough time to turn the arena over in time for the fans to celebrate on the court. It could be moved to a practice court,” she said via Oh No He Didn’t’s X . As she was talking about this possibility, Chiney Ogwumike couldn’t believe it. She held her head in disappointment and surprise and said, “you’re kidding me.” Ogwumike then smiled as the whole scenario just seemed bizarre. Fans were shocked when they realized it and held Cathy Engelbert accountable. “Unserious league,” one fan said . “This is ridiculous,” one fan said . The WNBA Commissioner has faced a lot of backlash this season. As she departs in December, the WNBA Finals have also drawn criticism of her leadership. Ramona Shelburne shares what would happen in a bizarre scenario Shelburne said winners’ celebrations could be cut short because of the Hawks game. “That celebration may not actually be on that court. I’ve heard there are discussions about whether there’s enough time to turn the arena over in time for the fans to celebrate on the court. It could be moved to a practice court,” she said via Oh No He Didn’t’s X . As she was talking about this possibility, Chiney Ogwumike couldn’t believe it. She held her head in disappointment and surprise and said, “you’re kidding me.” Ogwumike then smiled as the whole scenario just seemed bizarre. Read more: Atlanta Dream Coach Quips At WNBA’s Scheduling Decision For Dream vs Valkyries Game 6 “Stop the fake outrage” – Jason Whitlock Seemingly Takes Jab At Angel Reese Over WNBA Finals Game 6 Venue Drama College Sports Network has you covered with the latest news, analysis, insights, and trending stories in college football , men’s college basketball , women’s college basketball , and college baseball !

item.title: The Valkyries are one win away from a title after the Kiah Stokes game
item.description: Golden State Valkyries center Kiah Stokes knocks the ball away from Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese during the first half of Game 5 of the WNBA basketball finals in San Francisco, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Franci) For even the greatest players in the world, validation can be a beautiful thing and nobody knows it better than Kiah Stokes did on Monday. After a 64-55 Game 5 victory that put the Golden State Valkyries just completing their five-year championship journey three years ahead of schedule, Ballhalla serenaded the 11-year veteran with boisterous cheers and chants of M-V-P that drowned out the attempt to broadcast her on-court postgame interview to the arena. "It feels pretty special," Stokes told reporters about hearing the chants. "I always knew what I what I brought to a team, like I always understood my value, but just to hear like an arena full of 18,000 fans, it just really makes me feel appreciated and loved. I mean, there's not another way to say that." That response came on a follow-up about putting those cheers in the context her career in the WNBA. Just before that, she was as humble as could be - a personality trait that teammate Veronica Burton jokingly suggested was a fault - in noting how basketball is a team game and she's just one piece of that puzzle. But Golden State fans had every reason to deafen their neighbors in celebration over what they saw on the court Monday night. In a game where neither offense was able to pick up any sort of rhythm, Stokes was a near-perfect metronome, hitting the shots she was called upon to take, and doing so at a truly unprecedented level for her career. Now, statistically speaking, it doesn't take much to get into that unprecedented territory for Stokes in the Finals. Prior to this series against the Dream, the center's high mark in the title round was eight points in Game 2 of the 2023 Finals against the Liberty, and that was a 28-point victory that gave the Las Vegas Aces a 2-0 series lead. Stokes had already surpassed that during this Golden State playoff run, scoring nine in the Valkyries' historic Game 1 victory against the Dream, but followed that up with zero, two and four points in the next three games. Monday, though, Stokes ascended into double digits for the first time ever, tying for the team-high with 13 points. Even more remarkably, nine of them came from behind the arc as part of a 3-for-4 night from 3-point range, and when each one went in, it brought Ballhalla as close to absolute mayhem as they've been throughout their entire existence. This is not typical of what Stokes does. She's gone entire seasons scoring fewer than three 3-pointers, and had made just three in the 54 postseason games she checked in for prior to this, including two in that aforementioned 2023 Finals game. Kaitlyn Chen going nuts on the Valkyries bench after the Kiah Stokes three #WNBA https://t.co/D89cPB3qJS - Danielle H. (@DanielleHobeika) October 27, 20
item.content:encoded: Golden State Valkyries center Kiah Stokes knocks the ball away from Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese during the first half of Game 5 of the WNBA basketball finals in San Francisco, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Franci) For even the greatest players in the world, validation can be a beautiful thing and nobody knows it better than Kiah Stokes did on Monday. After a 64-55 Game 5 victory that put the Golden State Valkyries just completing their five-year championship journey three years ahead of schedule, Ballhalla serenaded the 11-year veteran with boisterous cheers and chants of M-V-P that drowned out the attempt to broadcast her on-court postgame interview to the arena. "It feels pretty special," Stokes told reporters about hearing the chants. "I always knew what I what I brought to a team, like I always understood my value, but just to hear like an arena full of 18,000 fans, it just really makes me feel appreciated and loved. I mean, there's not another way to say that." That response came on a follow-up about putting those cheers in the context her career in the WNBA. Just before that, she was as humble as could be - a personality trait that teammate Veronica Burton jokingly suggested was a fault - in noting how basketball is a team game and she's just one piece of that puzzle. But Golden State fans had every reason to deafen their neighbors in celebration over what they saw on the court Monday night. In a game where neither offense was able to pick up any sort of rhythm, Stokes was a near-perfect metronome, hitting the shots she was called upon to take, and doing so at a truly unprecedented level for her career. Now, statistically speaking, it doesn't take much to get into that unprecedented territory for Stokes in the Finals. Prior to this series against the Dream, the center's high mark in the title round was eight points in Game 2 of the 2023 Finals against the Liberty, and that was a 28-point victory that gave the Las Vegas Aces a 2-0 series lead. Stokes had already surpassed that during this Golden State playoff run, scoring nine in the Valkyries' historic Game 1 victory against the Dream, but followed that up with zero, two and four points in the next three games. Monday, though, Stokes ascended into double digits for the first time ever, tying for the team-high with 13 points. Even more remarkably, nine of them came from behind the arc as part of a 3-for-4 night from 3-point range, and when each one went in, it brought Ballhalla as close to absolute mayhem as they've been throughout their entire existence. This is not typical of what Stokes does. She's gone entire seasons scoring fewer than three 3-pointers, and had made just three in the 54 postseason games she checked in for prior to this, including two in that aforementioned 2023 Finals game. Kaitlyn Chen going nuts on the Valkyries bench after the Kiah Stokes three #WNBA https://t.co/D89cPB3qJS - Danielle H. (@DanielleHobeika) October 27, 2026 One person who didn't see this as anything new was head coach Natalie Nakase, who knows what Stokes is capable of at this stage because of her experience as an assistant in Las Vegas from 2022-2024. "Every day her habits are the same," Nakase told reporters of the veteran. "She takes over. She has a smile on her face. She studies the the game plan. She's always there, even with the highs and lows of the game. She just stays really composed... and now just shooting that three-ball like it's a lay-up. It was beautiful, and I love how the players today were just really trusting and moving the ball. Whoever was open, you know, got the shot." But a singular offensive explosion does not garner the full-throated MVP chants Stokes received at the buzzer. Anchor, stalwart, keystone, whatever go-to defensive descriptor one would want to use to describe her presence in the paint, and under the basket, is what she's delivered and then some. The physicality that brought complaints from Dream star Angel Reese and coach Karl Smesko emanates from her positioning down low and has helped the Valks get back to playing their game, one that turns a basketball game into a drunken slugfest in the mud. kiah stokes blocks and altered shots vs. angel reese https://t.co/YEuwWGsMeJ - jack maloney (@jackmaloneycbs) October 27, 2026 The numbers certainly back that up. Dream players defended by Stokes are being held to 9-for-48 from the field (0-for-8 from three) this series. Over the last two games, Stokes helped keep Reese to just 15 points on 4-of-20 shooting, silencing a player who was dictating how these Finals would be played, and possibly won, just five days ago. She also just tied the legend Lisa Leslie for the longest streak of games with three or more blocks in a single postseason with six. To Stokes, this just is the culmination of putting her head down and playing her game - "blue collar hoops" as she's referred to it. If Stokes' team needs a 3-point performance she's never put together before in her life, or to shut down one of the offensively potent opponents she's faced this postseason, then that's what she's going to give you. "You know, a lot of my game isn't really pretty," Stokes said, describing the phrase to reporters. "Do all the dirty work, rebounds, blocking shots, defense. But that's just what I know I could bring to the team. So whatever it takes to win." Today it's called "blue collar hoops," but as soon as Thursday it could be "Finals MVP hoops." More Valkyries - Love and grief turned a sports skeptic into a lifelong Valkyries fan - Fanatics prioritizing Caitlin Clark over Valkyries during WNBA Finals - Kaitlyn Chen is the Valkyries' 'goofy' secret weapon - Protesters showed up at the WNBA Finals. Valkyries fans shut them down. Full Valkyries coverage For all of our Bay Area sports coverage, sign up for The Catch newsletter . item.title: Bruno Fernandes: Ruben Amorim plotting to sink Man United even further with sensational January raid
item.description: Bruno Fernandes: Ruben Amorim plotting to sink Man United even further with sensational January raid Michael Carrick is not the only high-profile name at Manchester United whose future could lie away from Old Trafford. The Peoples Person has relayed that Bruno Fernandes might be the next superstar to leave following his recent spat with the head coach. The former United midfielder could be replaced by Eddie Howe , but the incoming manager could be given until next summer to work with the Portugal international . INEOS plan to let the 32-year-old leave , but only for the right price. The former Sporting CP attacking midfielder ‘s current United contract is valid until 2027. Bruno Fernandes on his way out However, the Red Devils plan to trigger their club captain’s one-year extension option to avoid losing him on a free. To do so, they need to act before the year ends, and Calciomercato have claimed that AC Milan are monitoring proceedings with interest. Former United boss Ruben Amorim, who is currently in charge of the team from the San Siro, is interested in reuniting with his compatriot as early as this winter. The Rossoneri will not find it easy to match United’s asking price, nor can they afford to pay Bruno Fernandes his current wages. The United No. 8 will need to reduce his demands if he is to move to Italy. AC Milan want Bruno Fernandes “Bruno Fernandes is a possibility but the Portuguese’s price tag remains high: his contract includes a foreign club clause worth nearly €65 million, and United, even if they fail to reach an agreement on a renewal, have the option to extend for another season. “However, the rift with the club could lead the player to force the issue and leave as early as January. Beyond the potential transfer costs, the Portuguese’s very high salary would still need to be taken into account: €10.2 million net per season, unmatched by AC Milan. “It would require a strong effort from both the player and AC Milan to find a solution.” Amorim is ready to make the United talisman the central cog in his plans to win over his former player, but they are not alone in the race. Galatasaray and Saudi Pro League sides are also expected to bid in January, and it will be interesting to see how this saga unfolds once a new head coach steps in. Feature image Julian Finney via Getty Images online polls

item.title: We can beat anybody, says Posh boss Savage
item.description: Robbie Savage was appointed Peterborough United boss on 2 October [Getty Images] Peterborough United boss Robbie Savage says his side "can beat anybody" as they prepare to face fellow League One club Bradford City in the last-16 tie of the Carabao Cup. Savage signed a "long-term" contract with Posh following his departure from National League club Forest Green Rovers earlier this month. The former Leicester City, Blackburn Rovers and Wales international midfielder has made a bright start to his time at London Road, losing just one of his first five matches in charge in all competitions. The highlight of his stint so far came in a 3-1 win at former club Leicester in his first league game, during which Peterborough ran into a three-goal lead at half-time. Having swept aside Championship side Watford 5-1 earlier in the League Cup under former boss Luke Williams, Posh have the opportunity to make the quarter-finals for the first time in 35 years when they travel to Bradford on Tuesday. Posh go into the tie as underdogs against a Bradford side which have not conceded a goal in almost eight hours of football in all competitions. "The lads are a great group, it's been an amazing start for them - one defeat in five, going to Leicester and winning, it's all come to fruition," Savage told BBC Look East. "Wouldn't it be great if we could go through and get a Premier League side in the quarter-final. "Financially, it would be great for the club. It would give the players a big boost going up against players they see week in, week out on the telly. "We've got a tough game against a Michael Duff side, he's a fantastic manager. They're a good side, but so are we. "We believe, as it stands, we can beat anybody." What can Posh fans expect from 'relentless' Savage? Robbie Savage: Colourful character set to spice up Posh Savage praises Posh attitude in Burton fightback MacAnthony denies Posh made illegal approach for Savage The influence that Savage has made on the side in his short reign so far should not be understated. Last season under Savage, Forest Green Rovers scored 82 league goals, but also conceded 52 times in the regular season before losing to Boreham Wood in the play-offs. Although Peterborough remain in the bottom four in League One, they are playing more attacking football and are consistently scoring late goals - including an equaliser in the 93rd minute at Bromley on Saturday. After taking on Bradford, Peterborough next travel to Luton on Saturday in the league. In a spooky coincidence, Savage faced the same opposition last Halloween when Forest Green fell to a thrilling 4-3 defeat by Luton in the FA Cup. After the match, the Welshman called it "one of the proudest moments of my footballing life". "Mine was always about proving people wrong and being the best I can be. "This group has the opportunity to be the best they can be - with a manager who believes in them." item.title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry has perfect reaction to Aaron Gordon getting ejected from Nuggets clash
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Warriors’ Stephen Curry has perfect reaction to Aaron Gordon getting ejected from Nuggets clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors played their hearts out on Monday night, earning a much-deserved 131-111 victory over the Denver Nuggets on the road. It looked like the Warriors already had the Nuggets on the ropes early in the fourth quarter, but Aaron Gordon ’s ejection after racking up two technical fouls in quick succession proved to be the final nail in Denver’s coffin on the night. With the Warriors up by 16, Nuggets forward Christian Braun got whistled for a push off on Stephen Curry before he set a screen on Brandin Podziemski. Gordon did not take too kindly to this, protested vehemently to the officials, and when he already got himself one technical foul, he pointed to the official — which sealed his ejection from this contest. Curry would then rub salt on the wound by pointing at Gordon before pointing to the tunnel to essentially say goodbye to the Nuggets forward. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steph Curry's reaction following Aaron Gordon's ejection 😅 pic.twitter.com/jhAS9f35Kh https://t.co/whup3jtvfr — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 27, 2026 The Warriors star just kept on finding ways to hurt the Nuggets on the night. He was as unselfish as it gets; even though he finished with just two assists, he released the ball early whenever Denver would blitz him on ball screens, and this would open up opportunities for the Dubs to attack four on three. Moreover, Curry did not force the issue on anything in this game. He shot the ball just eight times and he made all of his shot attempts to finish with 24 points. He did not have any issues with letting the young players, such as Yaxel Lendeborg, take over. Lendeborg finished with a career-high 31 points in a thorough decimation of the Nuggets’ defense. Meanwhile, Gordon had just seven points on 2-of-10 shooting from the field, which is quite lackluster considering his importance to this Nuggets offense. Curry, even at 38 years of age, showed just how important he remains to this Warriors team. He may not be the player he once was, but he remains the same level of threat to opposing defenses. His mere presence opens up so much space for his teammates, and he even inflicts emotional damage to the opposition. Related: Warriors’ Stephen Curry reveals the most impressive aspect of Yaxel Lendeborg’s game Related: Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg hits historic stat line only Victor Wembanyama matched as a rookie

item.title: 'Not trying to reinvent the wheel': Luke Williams backs Mumbai Indians' core for WPL 2027 | EXCLUSIVE
item.description: Mumbai Indians missed the Women’s Premier League playoffs last season after injuries and illness disrupted their combinations and close games slipped away. New head coach Luke Williams believes the franchise can return to contention without making wholesale changes to a side that has won two titles in four seasons. “Certainly not trying to reinvent the wheel,” Williams told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction from Adelaide. The Australian takes over from Lisa Keightley, who left after one season in charge. Keightley had succeeded Charlotte Edwards, who guided Mumbai to their inaugural WPL title in 2023. Williams knows Edwards from their time working in England’s women’s setup and arrives with a WPL title of his own, having coached Royal Challengers Bengaluru to the championship in 2024. He spent the 2026 season away from the competition, but when the Mumbai job became available, the prospect of returning to WPL - and working with Harmanpreet Kaur - appealed to him. “I was sort of, I guess, still a little bit surprised when it came about,” he said. “And from my end, I was extremely honoured and was interested straight away. Obviously, I've had some previous experience in the WPL. I had a year away from it last season and really missed being involved in the competition.” Mumbai are the two-time WPL winners, and Williams said the franchise’s record, along with the prospect of responding to a difficult campaign, made the role attractive. “The success that MI have had in all leagues, but also the WPL with two titles in the four years, was really exciting. And probably coming off a tougher year last year as well is a motivating factor to try and bounce back straight away and really compete for the title this year,” he said. Injuries, close games and the need for consistency Mumbai finished the 2026 league stage with three wins and five defeats, with Hayley Matthews missing the first three matches with a quad injury, while Nat Sciver-Brunt also dealt with illness. Harmanpreet scored 342 runs, Sciver-Brunt made 321, and Amelia Kerr took 14 wickets, but Mumbai could not convert enough individual performances into wins. Williams pointed to the difficulty of settling combinations in a tournament with only eight league matches. Mumbai lost close games, including their opening fixture against RCB, and had little time to recover from setbacks. “It looked like a challenging year with some injury and illness at different times. New head coach Luke Williams believes the franchise can return to contention without making wholesale changes to a side that has won two titles in four seasons. “Certainly not trying to reinvent the wheel,” Williams told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interaction from Adelaide. The Australian takes over from Lisa Keightley, who left after one season in charge. Keightley had succeeded Charlotte Edwards, who guided Mumbai to their inaugural WPL title in 2023. Williams knows Edwards from their time working in England’s women’s setup and arrives with a WPL title of his own, having coached Royal Challengers Bengaluru to the championship in 2024. He spent the 2026 season away from the competition, but when the Mumbai job became available, the prospect of returning to WPL - and working with Harmanpreet Kaur - appealed to him. “I was sort of, I guess, still a little bit surprised when it came about,” he said. “And from my end, I was extremely honoured and was interested straight away. Obviously, I've had some previous experience in the WPL. I had a year away from it last season and really missed being involved in the competition.” Mumbai are the two-time WPL winners, and Williams said the franchise’s record, along with the prospect of responding to a difficult campaign, made the role attractive. “The success that MI have had in all leagues, but also the WPL with two titles in the four years, was really exciting. And probably coming off a tougher year last year as well is a motivating factor to try and bounce back straight away and really compete for the title this year,” he said. Injuries, close games and the need for consistency Mumbai finished the 2026 league stage with three wins and five defeats, with Hayley Matthews missing the first three matches with a quad injury, while Nat Sciver-Brunt also dealt with illness. Harmanpreet scored 342 runs, Sciver-Brunt made 321, and Amelia Kerr took 14 wickets, but Mumbai could not convert enough individual performances into wins. Williams pointed to the difficulty of settling combinations in a tournament with only eight league matches. Mumbai lost close games, including their opening fixture against RCB, and had little time to recover from setbacks. “It looked like a challenging year with some injury and illness at different times. So trying to settle the combination down at different times is a big part of it. There were some close games, even the first game of the tournament against RCB. I think in this tournament where there's only eight games, close games are so important to try to get them to go in your direction. And try to win those crucial moments,” he said. “Still had a positive net run rate last year, I think. Mumbai and RCB were the only two teams to finish with a positive net run rate. So there's still a lot of positive signs. But just a couple of areas that we can hopefully have a bit of fortune with injury and illness. But also make sure that our processes, especially in the tighter games, are really clear and able to get over the line in those.” Williams does not intend to overhaul the team’s approach. He wants players to be clear about their responsibilities, while allowing for changes as their games develop between WPL seasons. “Primarily there's a lot to continue on with, I think, in terms of philosophy. But again, I guess [with] each player, it's a year between WPLs. So the players would have developed different things. So being really clear on their role within the side, where there might be some subtle shifts from different years with that,” he said. He pointed to the retentions as an indication of the franchise’s plans. “But again, in terms of the overall makeup, I think, or the composition, you could probably see from our retentions that we're keen to retain that core nucleus of the squad. But again, there may be some subtle changes to different roles and how we go about little bits and pieces. But certainly not trying to reinvent the wheel.” Harmanpreet stays on as captain Harmanpreet will continue to lead Mumbai, even as her international captaincy has ended. She stepped down as India captain this month, having led the team to its first Women’s Cricket World Cup title in 2025. For Williams, Harmanpreet remains central to his plans at Mumbai. The two have spoken online and over the phone and met during his recent visit to India. “Harman is obviously such an integral part of MI as well as Indian cricket, obviously. And will continue in the captaincy role and has just a huge presence within the franchise. Is really strong with her thoughts and beliefs and we're really aligned in how we want to take the team forward for not only this year but hopefully years to come,” Williams said. He values her ability to combine an intense competitive streak with composure when making decisions under pressure. “She's able to, I think, mix a steely sort of competitiveness and desire and all those attributes that you want to see in a leader, with still having a calmness and a game knowledge and an ability to make really good decisions under pressure,” he said. “So I love the combination of the leader that's there and stands up and always wants to compete, but also at the same time is able to be really calculated in the decisions that they make.” The auction: immediate needs and future options The WPL auction takes place in Kochi on October 28. Mumbai have retained Harmanpreet, Matthews, Sciver-Brunt and Kerr among others, giving Williams an experienced core to build around. His priority is to find players whose strengths complement those already in the squad, while ensuring the team has options for different pitches and conditions. “It's making sure that each person has some strengths that we feel can, I guess, be accentuated in our program, that will match well with other players that we've got, I guess, depending on the conditions that we're playing in, we've got options for wickets, whether they're turning wickets or slow wickets or whatever conditions we face, we've got a number of options to be able to do that,” he said. The search will not be limited to players expected to start every game. Williams also wants signings who can put pressure on the first-choice XI and step in when needed. “So we're in a really good position, I think, with a strong nucleus, experienced nucleus, but I think that's probably the primary function of the upcoming auction is to really be targeted in some players that we think can add, whether that's in the starting XI or putting pressure on or be ready to go if an opportunity presents,” he said. With the current WPL auction cycle entering its final year, immediate contribution will carry weight in recruitment. Williams said the franchise would nevertheless consider younger players who could remain part of the squad beyond the coming season. “Primarily in the last year of a cycle, you probably do lean towards immediate outputs and what the person can do in the next 12 months. That's probably certainly the initial lens that you look at players through,” he said. “But again, having a look at young players that may be able to be part of the franchise for a longer period of time, certainly cast an eye over that and be aware of that. And depending on how the auction goes or the person and how it unfolds, we're certainly open to that option as well to add to our list.” Data has its place, but players need to trust their game Williams has coached in the WPL and Australia’s Women’s Big Bash League, worked with England’s women’s team and been part of a title-winning Southern Brave staff in The Hundred. Across those environments, he said, preparation and confidence in individual roles remain central. “A lot of the same things are about making sure that your teams are as well-prepared as they possibly c

item.title: Israel Adesanya Finds New Motivation for UFC Comeback After Alexander Volkanovski’s UFC 333 Finish
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski once again silenced his doubters at UFC 333 , finishing Movsar Evloev in the second round to defend his featherweight title. The Aussie’s sharp striking and impressive takedown defense proved to be the difference as he handed the previously undefeated Russian his first career loss. With the victory, Volkanovski secured his ninth featherweight title fight win, surpassing Jose Aldo’s record. At 38, “Old Man Volk” delivered one of the most impressive performances of his career, and it seems his latest triumph has inspired Israel Adesanya to make a comeback of his own. Israel Adesanya Hails Alexander Volkanovski After Historic UFC 333 Title Win at 38 For the uninitiated, Adesanya is going through the toughest stretch of his MMA career. The former two-time middleweight champion is currently on a four-fight losing streak and made some major changes to his team earlier this year. In July, Adesanya announced that he was parting ways with longtime coach Eugene Bareman and City Kickboxing. His latest setback came against Joe Pyfer at UFC Seattle , where he was stopped in the second round after his opponent unleashed a brutal ground-and-pound attack. Adesanya’s last victory came in 2023, when he knocked out Alex Pereira in their rematch at UFC 287. Since then, the former champion has struggled to find his footing, going 1-5 in his last six fights. With many calling for him to retire, Adesanya has shown no intention of hanging up his gloves just yet. Watching his former City Kickboxing teammate finish an undefeated opponent at 38 appears to have given Izzy another reason to keep fighting. Reacting to Volkanovski’s performance in a video uploaded to his YouTube channel , Adesanya couldn’t hide his excitement. He said, “Let’s go, Volk! Let’s go, Volk. The best ever! F**k yeah. Legend. It’s legendary. All levels. Look at that. It (the finish) was early; I thought it was gonna be like round four.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by UFC on TNT Sports (@tntsportsufc) ALSO READ: Israel Adesanya Urges Alex Pereira to Return to 205lbs, Claims He Could Get an Immediate Title Shot Volkanovski’s dominant performance seemed to get Adesanya thinking about his own return to the Octagon. Clearly fired up by what he had just witnessed, Izzy exclaimed, “Look at him, just the blood. I can’t wait. Let me bang, bro. Just let me bang, bro.” Adesanya could soon get the opportunity to make a statement of his own. Rumors suggest that he could face Shara Magomedov at UFC Saudi Arabia on December 5 . While the event and matchup have yet to be officially announced, several reports have pointed to the potential clash as Adesanya’s next challenge. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ESPN MMA (@espnmma) With Volkanovski showing that age is no barrier to putting on a career-defining performance, Adesanya may be hoping to follow a similar path. Whether he can turn that inspiration into a much-needed win remains to be seen.

item.title: Steph Curry revs up for perfect night, watches as Warriors finish rout in Denver for first win
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, left, looks to pass the ball while under pressure from Denver Nuggets guard Christian Braun, right, in the first half of an NBA basketball game Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Denver. (AP Photo/David Zalubowski) (David Zalubowski/Associated Press) DENVER - You could feel the engine, from the minute the gas was pressed. Stephen Curry had a little extra, this night, after a month in Golden State with a tarp over the V12 only removed for test-drives around the block. He down-shifted off an early pick-and-roll in vintage form, hitting the turbo, hitting Brandin Podziemski for a left-wing 3-pointer as the Nuggets' defense caved in. The tarp came back on, quick. In the first half against Denver Monday night, Curry took exactly one shot in 14 minutes, a strangely passive effort from Golden State's star. Then, in the third quarter of Golden State's 134-114 win over Denver, the engine roared, as Curry looked as physically sound and quick as he has since the knee troubles that invaded last January. Hunting his own shot without forcing, and feeling a spark against a Nuggets team that visibly lacked much fire for three quarters, Curry let off a quiver of arrows at Ball Arena. He slashed. He quick-released over guard Christian Braun and his 6-foot-7 wingspan. He lost his dribble while checked by DeMar DeRozan, and flailed, and meandered, and turned a corner and dropped in another dime at the bucket, a four-point halftime lead suddenly pushed to 14 after another timeless show of Curry theatrics. Two weeks ago, Curry simply wasn't "where he ultimately wants to be" physically, as head coach Steve Kerr said. He dialed back his own summer work, took fewer reps training camp, and limited his preseason game action more than ever. The Warriors bubble-wrapped him, and Curry acquiesced, telling the Chronicle he was aiming for the "big picture." At some point, though, he needed unwrapping. And he took center stage in the second half in Denver, with a 17-point run in just 7:30 of game clock. He ended it perfect - 8-of-8 from the field and 5-of-5 from the free-throw line for 24 points, hopping and kicking and wiggling his hips. The Warriors failed in their home opener last Friday because there were few secondary options beyond a Curry- Draymond Green pick-and-roll that became simply too predictable . Their $57 million Robin, after all, is but a current presence in voice and in spirit, Jimmy Butler still nursing the knee injury that is hanging over Golden State's season. The workload on Curry's shoulders is heavier than ever, as his knees only add miles. He knows. "Take the shots when you're open - be aggressive, try to create, play-make," Curry said last Friday, to a question about fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski. "We need scoring from wherever we can get it, up and down the roster." In Denver, on Monday, the 23-year-old Podziemski looked like a man who listened. He began the night firing, with six of Golden State's first 11 attempts from the floor. He ended it as an irreplaceable connector, finishing with 18 points, seven rebounds, five assists and no turnovers, a game-high plus-30 in his 31 minutes of work. "There's a reason," Kerr said last Friday, "that we signed him to that contract." Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , meanwhile, picked up any slack available, repeatedly attacking the chest of Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon and three-time MVP Nikola Jokic. Denver had little answer for Lendeborg's aggressiveness in transition and as a ballhandler. The Warriors' ascending rookie sent home one fourth-quarter jam with a roar and a career-best 31 points to go with 12 rebounds and six assists. Golden State, too, managed the eminently difficult task of neutralizing Jokic behind Green - who started at center and stuck to the Nuggets star like plaque - and the 40-year-old Al Horford , who made Jokic pay for drop coverage on the other end with three 3-pointers. item.title: Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb reveals why he actually loves playing in Philadelphia
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb reveals why he actually loves playing in Philadelphia appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . CeeDee Lamb has plenty of reasons to enjoy playing for the Dallas Cowboys . However, his favorite NFL environment might surprise fans. After helping Dallas deliver a dominant 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, the superstar wide receiver revealed why he genuinely enjoys playing at Lincoln Financial Field. For Lamb, beating a familiar rival in its own building carries a special satisfaction. That makes the annual NFC East showdown his favorite matchup. Appearing on SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt, Lamb did not hesitate when asked where defeating Philadelphia ranked among his personal highlights. "I love playing [in Philadelphia]. … You always want to beat a brother." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) CeeDee Lamb joins @notthefakeSVP following the Cowboys' primetime win in Philly 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Wknnewm0L0 — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 27, 2026 “No. 1,” Lamb said. “I love playing here. You know what I’m saying, I am here once a year and it’s like very routine. This is like one of those, you always want to beat a brother.” Lamb added that the familiarity between the teams makes the rivalry especially challenging. He backed up those words with two touchdown receptions. Those included an acrobatic 16-yard connection with Dak Prescott that helped Dallas reclaim the lead in the third quarter. Lamb’s 2026 campaign has been outstanding despite Dallas’ uneven start. Through seven games, he has amassed 53 receptions for 651 yards and six touchdowns. His explosive performances have included a 17-catch, 189-yard outing against Houston and 100-yard games against Washington and Baltimore. His ability to command defensive attention has also helped create opportunities for George Pickens. Monday’s performance reinforced Lamb’s importance to Dallas’ postseason ambitions. The Cowboys used a strong second-half surge to pull away from Philadelphia. For Lamb, the hostile atmosphere is part of the appeal. And after another memorable night in Philadelphia, he has every reason to welcome the next trip back. Related: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott voices support for ‘pissed off’ Brian Schottenheimer Related: Cowboys’ Dak Prescott wears special shirt to postgame presser after MNF win over Eagles

item.title: Bam Adebayo Reacts After Terrible Game for Heat vs. Mavericks
item.description: Bam Adebayo Heat Mavericks Getty Miami Heat team captain Bam Adebayo reacted after having a terrible game against the Dallas Mavericks on Monday night. Adebayo scored just 8 points on 3-of-10 shooting, including going 0-of-5 from the 3-point range, as the Heat lost to the Mavericks 113-109. The Heat are now 0-4 on the year, and with the losses adding up, Adebayo’s struggles are getting magnified. Bam Adebayo Speaks After Heat Lose to Mavericks Speaking to reporters after the Heat lost to the Mavericks, Adebayo shared his reaction after another terrible game by himself and the team. “My shot’s not going in. I’m not going to overthink that. It’s funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat. When the energy shifts, be prepared for that,” Adebayo said. Bam Adebayo on his struggles 😳 "My shot's not going in. I'm not going to overthink that. It's funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat. When the energy shifts, be prepared for that" pic.twitter.com/YNX4FyxWVO — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) October 27, 2026 Adebayo’s comments about being made the team’s scapegoat are certainly interesting, as he doesn’t seem to really be taking any responsibility for his poor play, and is instead shooting it back at the critics. He even doubled down on his comments about the “outside noise,” suggesting that when the Heat eventually go on a win streak, the negative talk about the team will change. “I got expectations. Obviously the outside noise got outside expectations for us…. When we go on a 10 game win streak, then how does the noise change?” Adebayo said. Bam Adebayo on being the scape goat for this Heat team: "I got expectations. Obviously the outside noise got outside expectations for us…. When we go on a 10 game win streak, then how does the noise change?" https://t.co/obsYlyRUP1 pic.twitter.com/GKJUPouzK6 — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) October 27, 2026 Davion Mitchell Wants to Help Bam Adebayo Heat point guard Davion Mitchell, who has been one of the team’s best players in the early goings-on of the season, wants to help his center out by setting him up for better shots. However, Mitchell also thinks that Adebayo needs to learn how to space things better with Heat superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he and Adebayo have not been able to mesh as well as either the team or both players would have hoped. “I have to do a better job of not letting him get lost in the game, but he also has to be intentional. He gotta be more aggressive. Him and Giannis play in the same spaces so when Giannis is on the floor with him, he can’t be in those same spaces,” Mitchell said. Davion Mtichell on how he can help Bam get going: "I have to do a better job of not letting him get lost in the game, but he also has to be intentional. He gotta be more aggressive. Him and Giannis play in the same spaces so when Giannis is on the floor with him, he can't be in… pic.twitter.com/K97fDdfvbt — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) October 27, 2026 This article was

item.title: ‘Uh-Oh,’ ‘He’s Probably Not Too Happy With All of Us’ — Cowboys Media React to Brian Schottenheimer’s Terse Presser After Huge Win vs. Eagles
item.description: 'Uh-Oh,' 'He’s Probably Not Too Happy With All of Us' — Cowboys Media React to Brian Schottenheimer's Terse Presser After Huge Win vs. Eagles Brian Schottenheimer and the Dallas Cowboys finally had something to celebrate on Monday night. They beat divisional rivals Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 at Lincoln Financial Field to end a two-game losing streak and move to 3-4. However, the head coach didn’t have much to say about it. His postgame news conference lasted all of four minutes. It ended a week in which Schottenheimer faced criticism of his play-calling and publicly challenged receiver George Pickens over his blocking. Brian Schottenheimer Says Little After Cowboys Beat Eagles in Prime-Time The win looked very different from the two losses before this: a 24-16 home defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and a 23-13 road loss to the Green Bay Packers. On Monday, Dallas ran 38 times for 204 yards. Javonte Williams had 25 carries for 155 yards and a touchdown, becoming the first Cowboys RB since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018 to top 150 rushing yards. Dak Prescott completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to CeeDee Lamb, and the Cowboys didn’t commit a turnover. Pickens caught four passes for 57 yards, including a 21-yard touchdown in the second quarter. According to The Athletic’s Jon Machota, Schottenheimer “was very short with his postgame responses.” When the coach was asked whether everything was OK, he answered , “I’m great. Excited for our guys.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Others in Cowboys media also noticed how short it was. Shan Shariff, a “105.3 The Fan” host, needed one word: “Uh-oh.” Beat reporter RJ Ochoa had a different take , supporting Schottenheimer’s move: “Good for Schotty. Keep it tight. No need to say much at all about this. Consider it done. Lock it up. Move on to the next one. It is unfortunate if you are transparent like he is, but offering too much can create more harm than good sometimes. Seems he has learned that.” 105.3 The Fan, the home of the Cowboys’ radio, followed with a clip of Bryan Broaddus, Zach Wolchuk and Bobby Belt reacting to how short Schottenheimer had been with reporters. Broaddus said , “He’s probably not too happy with all of us right now,” while Belt noted that Schottenheimer “probably gets too much hate” but added, “he’s deserved all the hell he’s gotten the last couple of weeks.” Schottenheimer had plenty to say last week, with Dallas sitting at 2-4, which made him a target of criticism from former players and the media. item.title: What Rangers ‘must fix fast’ after Kings loss, per Mike Sullivan
item.description: Dennis Schneidler-Imagn Images What Rangers ‘must fix fast’ after Kings loss, per Mike Sullivan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin for the entire season earlier this month. Unfortunately, New York has not been able to recover on the ice without their elite goaltender. Head coach Mike Sullivan watched as his team fell on home ice to the Los Angeles Kings on Monday. The Rangers lost to the Kings by the score of 6-3. Defenseman Drew Doughty led the way, scoring three points. New York has now lost five of its last six games. Sullivan believes there are players who simply don’t have their heads in the game right now. “I just didn’t think from a mindset standpoint, I don’t think we had enough guys that were ready to play from the drop of the puck,” Sullivan said, via NHL.com. “We’ve got to fix that fast. The onus is on each individual to get himself ready for when the puck drops. It wasn’t everybody, but we just didn’t have enough.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Veteran journeyman James Reimer took the crease for the Rangers in this contest. Things did not go well for him, either. He allowed three goals on eight shots in the first period. Both of the first two shots he faced went in as well. The Rangers turned to primary starter Dylan Garand for the remainder of the game. Overall, it was a brutal loss for a Rangers team that needs to find ways to string together wins this season. New York will try to move on from this defeat. The Rangers will have time to clear their heads a bit, too. They take the ice again on November 1 against the Edmonton Oilers. Related: Rangers sign veteran James Reimer, give him immediate start vs. Kings Related: Rangers add veteran forward amid hot start to 2026-27

item.title: Eagles’ Jalen Carter Facing NFL Punishment for What He Did to Cowboys TE
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles DT Jalen Carter likely has a fine coming his way after striking Cowboys TE Berwyn Spann-Ford Getty ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 23: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles works against Cooper Beebe #56 of the Dallas Cowboys during a game at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter has a history of getting himself into trouble when he plays the Dallas Cowboys. Just last season, Carter was fined $57,222 and suspended for one game after spitting on Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott in the season opener. That incident seemingly solidified Carter’s reputation for being a dirty player. That reputation was highlighted again in Monday’s Week 7 matchup against the Cowboys on “Monday Night Football.” NFL Fine Likely After Jalen Carter-Brevyn Spann-Ford Incident Getty Philadelphia Eagles DT Jalen Carter struck Dallas Cowboys TE Berwyn Spann-Ford in the face and neck During the third quarter of Sunday’s game, with Dallas trailing 21-20, Carter drew more negative attention to himself with some over-aggressive behavior toward Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford . During a Javonte Williams run, Spann-Ford was tasked with blocking Carter. The two kept things going after the play was over when Carter struck Spann-Ford in the face and followed that up with another shove to his neck. Carter’s actions immediately caught the attention of “Monday Night Football” announcers Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, who pointed out Carter likely has a fine coming his way from the NFL . “Here’s Jalen Carter taking a shot at Brevyn Spann-Ford — a couple (of shots),” Aikman said. “He’ll be hearing from the league.” Carter wasn’t flagged on the play, but the NFL is likely to review the incident. A first-time offense for striking, kicking, tripping, or kneeing an opponent is $12,537. It escalates to $18,507 for a second offense. Carter hasn’t been fined this season, so his fine would be on the lighter side. Spann-Ford got the last laugh as the Cowboys scored on a 16-yard touchdown catch by CeeDee Lamb to take the 28-21 lead a few plays later. Carter has been fined five times during his NFL career: $11,473 for unnecessary roughness against the Kansas City Chiefs , Nov. 24, 2023 $16,937 for unnecessary roughness against the San Francisco 49ers , Dec. 8, 2023 $17,445 for open-handed blow to Tyler Biadasz in NFC Championship Game, Jan. 2025 $57,222 for spitting on Dak Prescott, Sept. 9, 2025 $11,593 for Taunting after blocking a field goal, Sept. 27, 2025 This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Eagles’ Jalen Carter Facing NFL Punishment for What He Did to Cowboys TE appeared first on HEAVY .

The side batting second won both matches in Christchurch, and India chased under the lights each time. The 8 pm starts and the heavy dew made the ball slippery for bowlers. The Blackcaps now reach Wellington missing two key seamers. Matt Henry has been rested for the remaining games, and Lockie Ferguson misses this particular contest. India’s batting order also contains a man who rarely lets a chase slip away. Tilak Varma has finished 26 T20 chases, and he hasn’t been on the losing side in any of them, which makes him an ideal player to have at the crease when the target is getting closer. item.title: Kirill Marchenko Injury Update: Why Maple Leafs’ New Winger Left Game vs. Flames
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - OCTOBER 20: Kirill Marchenko #86 of the Toronto Maple Leafs seen in action during the game against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Nationwide Arena on October 20, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Mowry/Getty Images) Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs made a bold move on the eve of this season. The day before they played their first game, the Leafs traded Matthew Knies in a blockbuster deal with the Columbus Blue Jackets that mainly brought aboard the athletic winger Kirill Marchenko. It was a risk for Toronto, but one they were willing to take. The Maple Leafs wanted to add firepower, so they took a chance. Marchenko has had impressive moments so far, but everything can change in an instant in the NHL, and that’s what happened Monday night as the Leafs took on the Calgary Flames and Marchenko had to leave the game. Kirill Marchenko Injury Update The Maple Leafs announced before the end of Monday’s game that Marchenko wouldn’t be returning on this night. He had headed to the locker room about 45 minutes before the Maple Leafs officially ruled Marchenko out. Marchenko got hurt when he was skating in the offensive zone and got tangled with a Calgary defender. The Leafs winger fell down, and his left leg got caught underneath him a little bit. His right leg also extended outward. There was lot of potential for muscular discomfort there. Watching the replay over and over, it’s reasonable to understand why Marchenko went to the locker room and didn’t come back into the game. Kirill Marchenko Stats Marchenko’s absence would hurt the Maple Leafs if that comes to fruition. So far this season, Marchenko had put up 14 points in 13 games, entering Monday night. That included six goals and eight assists. Marchenko also has 20 hits and five blocked shots in the early going of his first season with the Maple Leafs. Marchenko has generally been working on the second line with Nick Paul and William Nylander. If Toronto needs to promote someone into his place, the simplest move is Gavin McKenna, who plays on the left wing like Marchenko does. It remains to be seen just how bad the injury might be for Marchenko, though. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Kirill Marchenko Injury Update: Why Maple Leafs’ New Winger Left Game vs. Flames appeared first on HEAVY .

(Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 26: Tim Hardaway Jr. #10 of the Miami Heat drives against Walter Clayton Jr. #1 of the Dallas Mavericks during the fourth quarter of the game at Kaseya Center on October 26, 2026 in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) Getty The Dallas Mavericks beat the Miami Heat 113-109, sending the Heat to 0-4. Walter Clayton Jr. was waived by the Memphis Grizzlies on October 19th. Now with the Mavericks, Clayton is making an immediate impact for a team that needed a backup guard. Clayton finished with 15 points that may have shown the Mavericks that they found something with him as a backup guard. Mavericks Guard Walter Clayton Jr. Makes His Presence Known Getty MEMPHIS, TENNESSEE – MARCH 20: Walter Clayton Jr. #4 of the Memphis Grizzlies shoots a three-point shot in the fourth quarter against the Boston Celtics at FedExForum on March 20, 2026 in Memphis, Tennessee. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Matthew A. Smith/Getty Images) Clayton scored 15 points in 17 minutes and only missed one field goal. He was 6/7 and made both of his two three-point attempts. Clayton got in the game halfway through the second quarter and immediately got to work. He had five quick points and an assist to Cooper Flagg. Immediately, he showed how fearless he is and that he is a shooter that Dallas needs. He is able to create his own shot while also being a catch-and-shoot guy. His playmaking is also something that has been needed. He finished with five assists Saturday against the Spurs and four assists Monday against the Heat. Dallas has needed a playmaker and scorer off the bench, and now it’s looking like they have one. Clayton Complements the Starters Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA – OCTOBER 26: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks drives to the basket against Bam Adebayo #13 of the Miami Heat during the first quarter at Kaseya Center on October 26, 2026 in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) Clayton’s style of play is perfect for the way that the Mavericks want to play. They like playing fast and getting out and going. His 15 points were huge; without his scoring, Dallas would have lost this game and gone to 1-3. He made the starters’ jobs a lot easier because he is a player who finds the right spot to be in every time. Clayton’s 15 points really helped, as the starters were the main ones doing anything. Particularly, Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving , and P.J. Washington were the only ones scoring. Irving had 18, Washington had 20, and Flagg scored 29 points. They really needed Clayton’s production from the bench unit, and he provided. Clayton Could Earn a Bigger Role Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA – OCTOBER 26: Tim Hardaway Jr. #10 of the Miami Heat drives against Walter Clayton Jr. #1 of the Dallas Mavericks during the fourth quarter of the game at Kaseya Center on October 26, 2026 in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) This performance by Clayton is something that could potentially earn him a bigger role. His three-point shooting and playmaking is something that Dallas has desperately needed off the bench. If he can stay consistent and be a reliable shooter going forward, he will be their main guy off the bench. He has a really good opportunity to earn a lot of minutes and finally get his chance. He is currently on the Mavericks on a two-way contract and if he keeps playing like this could earn himself a guaranteed contract. The Jazz and Grizzlies didn’t give Clayton a chance; now Dallas is giving him his shot. He is showing that the other teams should have given him his opportunity. This was just one game, but he may have his minutes increased next game and have a bigger opportunity. The Mavericks are now 2-2, with one of those losses coming without Flagg and Irving. They don’t look like a bad team and now may have found a reliable bench piece. Clayton is now getting an opportunity to show what he’s capable of, and it’s up to him to keep making the best of it. He’s a good playmaker, three-point shooter, and defender, which is everything that Dallas needs. item.title: Je’Von Evans Makes History in Impromptu WWE Championship Match
item.description: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - SEPTEMBER 14: Je'Von Evans makes his entrance during Monday Night RAW at Arena Ciudad de Mexico on September 14, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Rich Freeda/WWE via Getty Images) Getty Rising WWE star Je’Von Evans added another milestone to his young career on Monday night, becoming the youngest wrestler to compete for the WWE Championship. Impressively, following his impromptu WWE Championship bout with Sami Zayn on RAW, Evans is also the youngest World Championship match participant in WWE history. Je’Von Evans, 22, surpassed the previous mark set by Randy Orton, who was 24 when he won the World Heavyweight Championship in 2004 at SummerSlam. Evans latest milestone continues what has been a historic year for the high-flyer. Evans has also staked his claim as the youngest Elimination Chamber and Money in the Bank Ladder match participant. He was the Iron Man of the 2026 Royal Rumble, surviving 41 minutes in the match to earn the honor. Je’Von Evans Makes History on RAW Just a few short weeks after suffering a 20-foot free-fall through an ambulance at Money in the Bank, Je’Von Evans was presented with a golden opportunity on RAW. RAW general manager Adam Pearce kicked off the show by announcing that Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan would compete later in the evening for the World Women’s Championship. Just as Pearce was about to make another announcement, he was interrupted by WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn, who demanded Pearce leave the ring so he could address the WWE Universe. Zayn noted that, despite being a two-time WWE Champion, he still feels largely underrated and underappreciated. The Canadian star added that he has also tolerated disrespect from his peers, and that he didn’t take too kindly to being interrupted by Je’Von Evans and Trick Williams in recent weeks. Just then, a confident Evans interrupted him once more. Evans stepped to the WWE Champion and dared him to finish his comments about him face-to-face. Following a heated exchange, Pearce returned from backstage and booked an impromptu WWE Championship match between the two stars. For Evans, it was his first championship opportunity since being promoted to the WWE main roster. The Monday night matchup was also his first match since suffering a 20-foot free-fall through an ambulance at Money in the Bank. Crazily enough, the last-minute championship bout nearly became a Triple Threat match. Bron Breakker Blocks Penta’s Cash-In Attempt Penta still has a year to cash in his MITB briefcase, but the luchador nearly pulled the trigger on Monday night. As Evans and Zayn traded blows, Penta entered the arena with his pyro-equipped briefcase. Penta walked toward the ring alongside a referee and seemed primed to cash in to make the match a Triple Threat. Suddenly, Bron Breakker stormed down the ramp and ambushed Penta before he could formally cash in. Je’Von Evans leaped outside of the ring to defend Penta from Breakker’s assault. Bron Breakker Blocks Penta’s Cash-In Attempt Penta still has a year to cash in his MITB briefcase, but the luchador nearly pulled the trigger on Monday night. As Evans and Zayn traded blows, Penta entered the arena with his pyro-equipped briefcase. Regarding Breakker, it will be interesting to see if he continues to hunt Penta. Still seething from his MITB loss, Breakker appears unwilling to let Penta cash in. He has also ambushed him in two of the last three weeks. Penta and Evans will get a shot at revenge at Crown Jewel, where they will face Bron Breakker and Austin Theory for the World Tag Team Championship.
