item.title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry pitches a perfect game in big win over the Nuggets
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Warriors’ Stephen Curry pitches a perfect game in big win over the Nuggets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Stephen Curry may be old , and he might sit out every back-to-back set the Golden State Warriors have this season. But on the games he suits up for, the expectation for Curry is that he’ll be his typically reliable self. He was exactly that on Monday as the Warriors earned their first win of the season in grand fashion by blowing out the Denver Nuggets, 134-114 . Curry recorded 24 points, three rebounds, and two assists, which is not even close to his biggest game ever. But he more than made up for it with his ridiculous shooting efficiency. The Warriors star made all eight of his field-goal attempts on the night (including a perfect 3-of-3 from deep), and he also made all five of his free-throw attempts, pitching a perfect game, so to speak, in the process. According to ClutchPoints’ Tomer Azarly, this is only the second time in Curry’s career in which he finished a game shooting 100% from the field. His first 100% FG game came all the way back in 2011, when the sophomore version of Curry put up 14 points on 5-of-5 shooting (3-of-3 from three) in a 102-89 victory over the New Orleans Hornets. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) What made this such a masterclass for Curry is that the Nuggets were selling out to make his life difficult. They were blitzing him on ball screens in an attempt to get the ball out of his hands, but the ball was making its way back to him and he made Denver pay. Even at 38 years of age, Curry’s mere presence opens up so much space for his teammates to do damage. On Monday, it was Yaxel Lendeborg who had himself a night. The 11th pick of the 2026 NBA Draft recorded a career-high 31 points to go along with 12 rebounds and six assists, and everything just becomes so much easier for the Dubs when Curry is healthy and humming. But another tough matchup awaits the Warriors. Their next game will be on Wednesday against the Minnesota Timberwolves, and that will be a road game as well. Related: Warriors’ Stephen Curry reveals the most impressive aspect of Yaxel Lendeborg’s game Related: Warriors’ Stephen Curry has perfect reaction to Aaron Gordon getting ejected from Nuggets clash

item.title: We’re here for NWSL Decision Day chaos. Plus: Putellas wins the Ballon d’Or
item.description: Full Time Newsletter ⚽| This is The Athletic ’s weekly women’s soccer newsletter. Sign up here to receive Full Time directly in your inbox. Seems like a good time to rewatch our sit-down with Alexia Putellas . Coming up today: 🏃‍♀️ Sprint to the NWSL playoffs 👋 Goodbye “Rodman Rule”’ 🏆 What makes an MVP? But first, breaking news … Golden: Putellas wins third Ballon d’Or If you wanted to predict the winner of the Ballon d’Or, always bet on Barcelona. Putellas collected her record-tying third Ballon d’Or today after leading Barcelona to a quadruple-title season last year. The 32-year-old spent 14 years at Barcelona before moving to London City last summer. She won her first two Ballons d’Or at 27 and 28 years old before suffering an ACL tear in 2022. She came back and helped Spain win a World Cup in 2023 and reached more than 200 goals for Barcelona in more than 500 appearances. The evening, co-organized by the France Football magazine and UEFA, is soccer’s red carpet moment of the year. To her credit, Putellas fully earned this year’s title under the current judging process. But that doesn’t mean we can’t expand our thinking beyond Europe when it comes to this global award. At least Temwa Chawinga made it into the top 10! Some notes before we move on: Barcelona manager Pere Romeu won coach of the year. No surprise there. You’ll never guess what his parents did for a living. We asked 30 former and current players, coaches and executives to vote for a Ballon d’Or Feminin winner. Spoiler: It wasn’t Putellas. Former voters who have been through the process explained why picking the best in the world is so difficult in the women’s game. There is a small fourth-tier club in Mallorca responsible for three Ballon d’Or nominees. We found out the secret to their success. Final Push Setting NWSL’s stage The penultimate episode of any good television series is full of drama. It’s when all of the loose ends get set on fire, the car chase hits max speed and the suspense sends chills down the spine. It sets up the finale to provide resolution and decompression. Similarly, the excitement of week 29 of 30 in the NWSL regular season started Friday when Portland defeated North Carolina with an absolute banger from Marie Muller in the 60th minute — struck right through the laces. The victory clinched a playoff berth for the Thorns and three other teams. Yesterday, Gotham could practically see their first NWSL Shield headed their way. The league leaders in points needed to beat Orlando ✅, hope for Kansas City to defeat Washington ✅ and root for geographical rival Boston to defeat San Diego ❌. Already eliminated from postseason contention, the Legacy nearly gifted Gotham the trophy by striking first, but San Diego forced two goals early in the second half that Boston could only match, not overcome. Seems like a good time to rewatch our sit-down with Alexia Putellas . Coming up today: 🏃‍♀️ Sprint to the NWSL playoffs 👋 Goodbye “Rodman Rule”’ 🏆 What makes an MVP? But first, breaking news … Golden: Putellas wins third Ballon d’Or If you wanted to predict the winner of the Ballon d’Or, always bet on Barcelona. Putellas collected her record-tying third Ballon d’Or today after leading Barcelona to a quadruple-title season last year. The 32-year-old spent 14 years at Barcelona before moving to London City last summer. She won her first two Ballons d’Or at 27 and 28 years old before suffering an ACL tear in 2022. She came back and helped Spain win a World Cup in 2023 and reached more than 200 goals for Barcelona in more than 500 appearances. The evening, co-organized by the France Football magazine and UEFA, is soccer’s red carpet moment of the year. To her credit, Putellas fully earned this year’s title under the current judging process. But that doesn’t mean we can’t expand our thinking beyond Europe when it comes to this global award. At least Temwa Chawinga made it into the top 10! Some notes before we move on: Barcelona manager Pere Romeu won coach of the year. No surprise there. You’ll never guess what his parents did for a living. We asked 30 former and current players, coaches and executives to vote for a Ballon d’Or Feminin winner. Spoiler: It wasn’t Putellas. Former voters who have been through the process explained why picking the best in the world is so difficult in the women’s game. There is a small fourth-tier club in Mallorca responsible for three Ballon d’Or nominees. We found out the secret to their success. Final Push Setting NWSL’s stage The penultimate episode of any good television series is full of drama. It’s when all of the loose ends get set on fire, the car chase hits max speed and the suspense sends chills down the spine. It sets up the finale to provide resolution and decompression. Similarly, the excitement of week 29 of 30 in the NWSL regular season started Friday when Portland defeated North Carolina with an absolute banger from Marie Muller in the 60th minute — struck right through the laces. The victory clinched a playoff berth for the Thorns and three other teams. Yesterday, Gotham could practically see their first NWSL Shield headed their way. The league leaders in points needed to beat Orlando ✅, hope for Kansas City to defeat Washington ✅ and root for geographical rival Boston to defeat San Diego ❌. Already eliminated from postseason contention, the Legacy nearly gifted Gotham the trophy by striking first, but San Diego forced two goals early in the second half that Boston could only match, not overcome. And so ended New York/New Jersey’s one day as Boston’s biggest fan. For the fifth time in league history, the Shield race comes down to the final day. There is also still one more playoff spot to book, as well as a home quarterfinal match to secure. Oh, and Courage midfielder Ashley Sanchez has just one more match day to try to beat Chawinga’s single-season scoring record. She’s just one goal away. In other words, Decision Day is once again going to be nuts . Bring on Decision Day If all of that isn’t enough drama for you, how about simultaneous kickoff times? All eight games commence at 5 p.m. ET on Sunday and will be broadcast across ESPN platforms. Gotham will get top billing on ESPN and ESPN Deportes. All other games air on ESPN+. ESPN 2 will provide the RedZone experience, with a live whip-around show starting at the same time. If that’s not your thing, here’s a helpful watch guide from Meg: For the Shield race: Gotham FC host Utah Royals FC San Diego Wave at Bay FC Gotham will clinch the Shield with a win or a draw against Utah. If Gotham loses, San Diego still needs to beat Bay to steal the Shield on the final day. For playoff hosting stakes: Washington Spirit host Chicago Stars KC Current at Racing Louisville Angel City host the Boston Legacy (in Carson, Calif., at Dignity Health Sports Park due to MLS scheduling) Utah Royals at Gotham FC For the final playoff spot: Seattle Reign host Orlando Pride North Carolina Courage host Denver Summit The Reign, eighth in the table , control their own destiny with 44 points, two ahead of the Courage and three ahead of the Summit. That makes North Carolina versus Denver the must-see match of the day . The only game without one of those stakes — but that will still determine quarterfinal matchup pairings — is the Thorns at Houston. Portland has lost the tiebreak based on total wins against Utah, but could still move up the table if Utah and/or Angel City lose. Every match matters, with meaningful stakes for the 10 remaining teams still in playoff contention. We’ll be right there with you for what promises to be a chaotic two hours (plus stoppage time). Meg’s Corner: NWSL Decision Day is a gift Please know that this is me heading into Decision Day: To be fair, I can fully enjoy what should be the league’s best regular-season finale yet, with 16 teams playing and every top-10 team playing for something, thanks to my neutral status after years of covering the league. Some narratives may be more appetizing than others, but with the Shield race, the final playoff spot and hosting privileges all on the line, two hours of glorious, chaotic NWSL action next Sunday are what I’m rooting for. This is exactly what the league has to be rooting for, too. With so much on the line, Decision Day is a perfect entry point for casuals and USWNT-only watchers — instant stakes leading into the playoffs. November nuttiness? November nonsense? We can workshop the NWSL version of March Madness, but the league needs to take advantage of this gift the 2026 season has provided. At the same time, I’ll be sending out good vibes for everyone’s stress levels. If you’re a fan, you might be able to appreciate the drama, but that doesn’t mean you’re going to have a good time. Good for the head, hard on the heart: Such is the glory and suffering of sports fandom. As for me? I’m ready to hit full NWSL sicko mode. Bring it on. News to Know Goodbye HIP, we hardly knew you Honestly, I have salad dressing with longer expiration dates than the NWSL’s “Rodman Rule.” I don’t know if that says more about me and my non-organic choices or the league. Either way, the NWSL got rid of the criteria for its High Impact Player rule as part of a wide-ranging settlement with the players’ association last week. Previously, players had to meet specific commercial or sporting criteria to qualify to have their salaries covered by an additional $1 million fund outside the salary cap. Roughly 100 players qualified. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr was one of the notable players who didn’t fit in that box. Though the criteria are gone, HIP will carry on as a way for teams to access funds once they’ve hit the salary cap — but the league maintains that this is NOT a raise to the salary cap itself, which would require revisiting negotiations with the PA. It’s worth your time to read the full breakdown of changes that came from the settlement, including updates to the controversial shoe brand deal. More news Columbus announced a 45,000-square-foot training facility today for its women’s team, joining the NWSL in 2028. Whitney Haslam Johnson, general manager of Haslam Sports Group, which owns the team, spoke to Asli Pelit about the plans, potential rivalries and who the team plans to sign. Tottenham fell 2-1 to Arsenal in the North London Derby on Saturday after Arsenal was awarded a controversial second-half penalty. Spurs coach Martin Ho called for increased refereeing standards in the WSL, saying the situation “has got worse.” Current midfielder Croix Bethune drips with style, so it’s no surprise her assist record-setting pass was against her forme

item.title: Petr Yan vs. Song Yadong 2 Betting Odds Revealed
item.description: Song Yadong Petr Yan Getty The betting odds for a potential rematch between UFC bantamweight champion Petr Yan and rival Song Yadong have been revealed. After Yan defeated Merab Dvalishvili in their trilogy bout in the co-main event of UFC 333, UFC commentator Daniel Cormier immediately asked him about a rematch against Song, who was sitting cageside watching the fight go down. While the UFC may ultimately choose a rematch with Sean O’Malley for Yan’s next fight, a rematch against Song cannot be ruled out, and now, we have the betting odds for this potential fight in case it gets booked. Betting Odds for Song Yadong vs. Petr Yan 2 Check out the betting odds for a potential rematch between Song and Yan. Petr Yan -250 Song Yadong +170 Future Fights Opening Odds: Song Yadong (+170)Petr Yan (-250) https://t.co/zY9fS9av5x #FutureFights — FightOdds.io (@FightOdds_io) October 24, 2026 Petr Yan Won the 1st Matchup Against Song Yadong Yan and Song first met back in March 2024 at UFC 299 in a three-round, non-title bout, a fight that Yan won via unanimous decision, with all three judges scoring that contest 29-28 in Yan’s favor. Statistically, it was a closely fought bout, as Yan landed 99 strikes to Yan’s 86, while Yan had two takedowns compared to just one for Song. Now, nearly three years later, these two rivals may meet for a second time if the UFC chooses Song as Yan’s next challenger. Working for Song is the fact that he is coming off an incredible upset KO win over Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC Shanghai in August, the biggest win of his career, as he took out one of the sport’s best bantamweights in a brutal fashion. It also helps that Song is Chinese, a market that the UFC is trying to capture, so it would give him an added boost in his title shot chances. Working against Song, however, is the fact that he already lost to Yan. As well, O’Malley has beaten Yan, and O’Malley has also beaten Song. That fight took place earlier this year, in fact, when he defeated him via unanimous decision at UFC 324. So that is working against Song, too. But if Song does get the title shot, then we know he will be the underdog against Yan. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Petr Yan vs. Song Yadong 2 Betting Odds Revealed appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Eagles’ Saquon Barkley reveals when he tweaked his hamstring on MNF vs. Cowboys
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Eagles’ Saquon Barkley reveals when he tweaked his hamstring on MNF vs. Cowboys appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles ’ Monday Night Football matchup against the Dallas Cowboys brought another disappointment as Philadelphia suffered five consecutive losses for the first time in 10 years. Moreover, running back Saquon Barkley ’s injury scare added to the frustration among Eagles fans. The star running back has now revealed when he first tweaked his hamstring during Monday’s game. Following the game, Barkley expressed his frustration over the recurring injury concerns. “I don’t know, I don’t get it,” Barkley said. “I just gotta find a way to get healthy. It’s annoying, but that’s what the season is, that’s what I’m dealing with so far in the season. I just gotta find a way to get healthy.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Barkley then said the injury happened during one of his early carries against Dallas and recalled feeling his leg being pulled during the play. “I mean, the first play, or I don’t know. One of my first runs, my head just opened up. I kinda got pulled a little bit, and didn’t really do too much. But that’s how the body works. Sometimes, something’s a little banged up; you’ll compensate a little bit.” Barkley entered the Week 7 matchup determined to help the Eagles snap their losing streak after missing their previous two games because of a hamstring injury. Barkley’s latest injury concern comes at a challenging time for Philadelphia, which has struggled to find consistency while dealing with a series of setbacks. The Eagles are also without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season because of blood clots, as well as wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. However, Barkley made an immediate impact upon returning to the lineup, helping the Eagles establish early momentum on offense. The running back recorded a rushing touchdown and accumulated 62 yards on seven carries. Philadelphia will hope Barkley’s latest injury is not serious, especially considering his importance to an offense that has struggled in his absence. However, until the team provides a further update on his condition, his availability for the upcoming game remains uncertain. Related: Eagle’ Riq Woolen, Jalen Carter decline to speak to the media after MNF loss to Cowboys Related: Eagles’ Saquon Barkley opens up on taking leadership role amid Philly’s woes

item.title: Cowboys pull a Meek Mill move Eagles fans won’t appreciate
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Cowboys pull a Meek Mill move Eagles fans won’t appreciate appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys kept on trying to win against the Philadelphia Eagles even after the game ended on Monday. Following the Cowboys’ 38-21 beatdown of Philadelphia in a Monday Night Football showdown at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, the sound of Meek Mill ’s ‘Dreams and Nightmares’ could be heard blaring from the visiting team’s locker room. Meek Mill blasting as Cowboys enter their locker room pic.twitter.com/NjNXpy3efJ — Kimberley A. Martin (@ByKimberleyA) October 27, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That song has become a rallying anthem for the Eagles, but it surely doesn’t sound right coming from a visiting team’s locker room, especially when that team is an NFC East rival. But the intention behind why the Cowboys played that song wasn’t really a big secret. They simply were cherishing a huge win against a bitter division rival. The game was close until the second half, when the Cowboys scored 18 points to Philadelphia’s seven. Dallas star quarterback Dak Prescott passed for 212 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions on 15-of-27 completions, while running back Javonte Williams had a night himself. Williams gashed the Eagles’ defense for 155 rushing yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. Meanwhile, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb caught two touchdowns for the Cowboys, who snapped a two-game losing skid and improved to 3-4. As for the Eagles, they just couldn’t get it together for an entire game. Tanner McKee started again with Jalen Hurts down for the rest of the season, and he went 23-of-35 for 211 passing yards and a touchdown plus an interception. The loss was the Eagles’ fifth in a row and dropped them to 2-5. The Cowboys return to action in a Week 8 game against the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. Related: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott voices support for ‘pissed off’ Brian Schottenheimer Related: Cowboys’ Dak Prescott wears special shirt to postgame presser after MNF win over Eagles

item.title: Angel Reese’s Fans Need to Answer One Question
item.description: Oct 26, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) motions to the referee after a foul call in favor of the Golden State Valkyries in the first quarter in game five of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images IF ANGEL REESE IS ALREADY A SUPERSTAR, WHY DOES EVERY CRITICISM TURN INTO AN EXCUSE? This is where the Angel Reese debate gets interesting. When Reese dominates the glass, her fans point to the numbers. When she puts together a huge scoring performance, they celebrate her potential. When she struggles, the conversation often shifts to her teammates, the opposing defense or people supposedly rooting against her. So which is it? Reese deserves credit for helping Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals. Her 30-point, 16-rebound performance in Game 2 showed exactly how dangerous she can be. But Monday night was a different story. She scored seven points as the Dream lost 64-55 to Golden State. Atlanta now faces elimination, and the pressure is only getting bigger. Nobody expects one player to win a championship alone. The Dream have plenty of questions to answer, and their overall offensive production has been a problem. Still, being a star means accepting scrutiny when things go wrong. You cannot demand superstar recognition while treating every tough question like a personal attack. And this isn’t about whether Reese is popular or polarizing. It’s about whether her basketball performances deserve the same honest evaluation as everyone else’s. HERE’S THE QUESTION THAT WILL MAKE BOTH SIDES MAD: If Angel Reese played for a team you didn’t care about, would you rate her basketball game exactly the same way? If your answer is yes, explain why. If your answer is no, explain that, too. Let’s see who can actually separate basketball from fandom. 👇

item.title: Watch: Cowboys insiders break down Dallas' desperately needed Monday night win over Eagles
item.description: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Ceedee Lamb (88) celebrates his touchdown reception with quarterback Dak Prescott (4) during the first half of an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Philadelphia. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) The Dallas Cowboys' season is not dead yet . They said they weren't desperate, but Dallas needed this 38-21 win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Cowboys insiders Calvin Watkins and Joseph Hoyt got together to share their thoughts on the Cowboys' performance in Week 7 . The Cowboys' running game was ignited at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday by Javonte Williams who rushed for a career-high in yards. DeMarvion Overshown's return from injury was also a highlight. item.title: Eagles' Defense Struggles in Blowout Loss to Cowboys
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles' rough season is continuing, as they were blown out by the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night, losing 38-21. Philadelphia's defense struggled to contain Dallas's explosive offense. Cowboys running back Javonte Williams had a career day, rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. As a team, Dallas rushed for 204 yards and a touchdown on 38 carries (5.4 yards per carry). The Cowboys also had success through the air, as Dak Prescott completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions. CeeDee Lamb was a tough cover, as he had five receptions for 74 yards and two touchdowns, while George Pickens had four receptions for 57 yards and a touchdown. Although the Eagles are facing many injuries to key players, it was still a disappointing performance from their defense. Philadelphia did not record a sack or tackle for loss, as they constantly loss at the line of scrimmage. The Eagles didn't have their best offensive performance either. Saquon Barkley rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown, along with two receptions for nine yards, but he dealt with multiple injuries during the game. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Their other running back, Dameon Pierce, had 47 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries, but went to the locker room in the fourth quarter. The injuries are continuing to pile up for the Eagles in what has been a very underwhelming season. In the passing game, backup quarterback Tanner McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. They were without two of their top receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, which allowed rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon to have a strong performance. Lemon had seven receptions for 67 yards and a touchdown, finally showing that he can be a key piece for Philadelphia on offense. Tight end Dallas Goedert was also solid with five receptions for 48 yards. Overall, the Eagles had a rough performance, as it's always difficult to lose to a division rival. Although the NFC East has been a wide-open division, Philadelphia has a plethora of injuries, and they are more likely to be sellers at the trade deadline than to compete for a playoff spot. The Eagles will head on the road to take on the Washington Commanders on Sunday in what is turning into a rebuilding and gap year for Philadelphia just two seasons removed from winning the Super Bowl.

item.title: ‘Defense Will Be Their Kryptonite,’ ‘Only Temporarily Masks The Truth’ — NFL Analysts Outline Why Cowboys’ MNF Win vs. Eagles Isn’t Moving The Needle
item.description: ‘Defense Will Be Their Kryptonite,’ ‘Only Temporarily Masks The Truth’ — NFL Analysts Outline Why Cowboys’ MNF Win vs. Eagles Isn’t Moving The Needle The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night to hand the Eagles their fifth straight loss. The Cowboys snapped a two-game losing streak against their NFC East rivals and improved to 3-4 on the season to round off the Week 7 slate. With Dallas preparing to host the Arizona Cardinals next Sunday, it will have another opportunity to build momentum after the Eagles win. item.content:encoded: ‘Defense Will Be Their Kryptonite,’ ‘Only Temporarily Masks The Truth’ — NFL Analysts Outline Why Cowboys’ MNF Win vs. Eagles Isn’t Moving The Needle The Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles 38-21 on Monday night to hand the Eagles their fifth straight loss. The Cowboys snapped a two-game losing streak against their NFC East rivals and improved to 3-4 on the season to round off the Week 7 slate. With Dallas preparing to host the Arizona Cardinals next Sunday, it will have another opportunity to build momentum after the Eagles win. However, several NFL analysts remain unconvinced about the Cowboys’ long-term prospects, raising questions about whether this win reflects a genuine turnaround. NFL Analysts Deliver Blunt Verdict on Cowboys After Win Over Eagles The New York Giants currently sit atop the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record, but the Cowboys kept themselves in the division title race by defeating the Eagles, giving them a chance to challenge for the top spot. Dak Prescott completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns without a single interception, while CeeDee Lamb finished with five catches for 74 yards and two scores. Javonte Williams also played a crucial role on the ground, rushing for 155 yards and scoring a late touchdown to help secure the win. He became the first Cowboys RB to top 150 rushing yards since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. However, many, including PFN Deputy Editor Alex Kennedy, remain unconvinced that Dallas can emerge as a serious contender. “The Cowboys have a chance to win the weak NFC East, but that isn’t saying much,” Kennedy said. “At the end of the day, their defense and coaching are holding them back from being true contenders. Barring massive improvements in those areas, this team isn’t making a playoff run.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor PFN analyst Jason Katz also thinks the Cowboys needed to “not just win, but win convincingly,” and the Eagles’ win didn’t prove their caliber. “It was close for a while, but they did exactly that,” Katz said. “This defense still has massive issues and will ultimately be their downfall, but the division is very much within reach,” Katz said. “Dallas has a favorable schedule coming up the next handful of games and needs to win the games they are supposed to win. Jacoby Brissett had exactly one win as a starter last season – against the Cowboys. They cannot let history repeat itself in Week 8.” PFN analyst Kyle Soppe believes the Eagles-Cowboys game did little to change his overall assessment of the NFC. “Technically, other divisions will be represented, but this conference, the NFC, has two live divisions and two dead ones, and this game did nothing to change my stance on that,” Soppe said. “The East name-brand teams are thrift-shop quality of play. Dallas won a game they needed tonight, but in terms of outlook come January? I’m going to need more than a multi-score win over Tanner McKee without his top receivers.” Dallas’ rushing attack was productive on Monday, but Philadelphia also found success on the ground. Saquon Barkley gained 62 yards on just seven carries, while Dameon Pierce added another 47 rushing yards and a score. Dallas also struggled to get off the field on third downs, and Philadelphia put together a 17-play drive that lasted more than nine minutes. The Eagles managed to sustain their offense despite relying on a backup quarterback and a banged-up offensive line. Those issues have left Jacob Infante concerned about the Cowboys’ defensive reliability. “The Cowboys have the explosive capability on offense to score in bunches, and that will keep them competitive in a lot of games,” Infante wrote. “That defense still remains questionable, since I won’t overreact to how they played against a hobbled Eagles offense. “I think they’re certainly more talented on paper than the Giants when you factor in the injuries that New York has, but the coaching element is where I think the Giants have the upper hand, and that should place them as the favorites in the NFC East above Dallas.” Ian Cummings also offered a similarly skeptical assessment. “A lot might be made of this game simply because it’s a primetime matchup and Dallas did win relatively convincingly, but in my opinion, it only temporarily masks the truth,” Cummings remarked. “Dallas still has massive flaws, particularly with their defense and their situational coaching and game management, and even if they’re still in reach of the NFC East, that’s the equivalent of the ‘NFC South’ award the past few years.” PFN analyst Brandon Astreicher also called out the Dallas defense, which ranks at the bottom of the league with a 61.4 PFN Defense Impact grade. “I think Dallas can definitely win the NFC East with how weak it is this season,” Astreicher said. “This defense will be their kryptonite when it’s time to play good offenses, but for now, they can win some games if their offense balls out and their defense plays just okay. “They couldn’t stop Saquon Barkley tonight, who looked hampered by his hamstring, so I can’t expect them to stop an offense like the 49ers or Bears when it matters. They could make some noise now, but it’s only a matter of time before a team plays silencer.” PFN analyst Brandon Austin also acknowledged the Cowboys’ offensive potential while expressing reservations about their overall outlook. “The Cowboys’ offense can hang with anybody, but we knew that already,” Austin said. “Hard to have any confidence in a team with a defense that hadn’t shown any signs of life until facing an Eagles offense featuring backups.” The win keeps Dallas firmly in the NFC East conversation, but improving its pass rush, coverage, and situational execution will be essential if the Cowboys hope to turn their offensive success into a genuine postseason run. item.title: Why Devin Booker Scored 3 Points for Suns vs. Thunder
item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA - OCTOBER 26: Devin Booker #15 of the Phoenix Suns handles the ball while being defended by Kenrich Williams and Jared McCain #3 of the Oklahoma City Thunder during the first half at Paycom Center on October 26, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Getty The Phoenix Suns faced a tall task on Monday night against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Nowhere was that more apparent than Devin Booker’s final stats in the 125-114 win for OKC over the Suns. Booker scored just three points. It’s the kind of line that makes you do a double take. The Suns’ star played 34 minutes but ended with just three points. How is that even possible? Well, here’s how. How Devin Booker Scored 3 Points Booker’s problem comes back to a few different things. We can start with the obvious — he attempted just seven shots from the floor in 34 minutes. He made one of those, actually a 2-pointer with a foul, and he added the free throw on his only attempt from the line. That’s how Booker got three points. So he was 1-for-7 from the floor, 0-for-2 from 3 and 1-for-1 from the line. That’s not enough shot attempts for Booker. The Suns had Miles Bridges take 17, Dillon Brooks take 14, Jalen Green take 13 and even Khaman Maluach shoot 10 times. Jordan Goodwin and Collin Gillespie each shot nine times off the bench. If Booker isn’t going to get chances to shoot the ball, or not going to shoot it when chances present themselves, the Suns are going to have a long season. Booker did take it upon himself to be the lead distributor on Monday night. He dished out a team-high seven assists. He added two rebounds, one steal and didn’t even turn the ball over once — so he did some good things. But overall, Booker was a minus-11, and the Suns lost to fall to 1-2. They’ve got a highly regarded defense, led on the perimeter by superstar guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who is a difficult guard to handle when he’s defending you. They actually only got nine minutes from Alex Caruso before he got hurt, so it might’ve been even tougher for Booker if that didn’t happen. The likes of Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain have both done their best to stay bought in defensively, too, but there are a lot of moving parts during the season. The reality is that Booker’s performance was more about him. He could’ve forced shots more. He didn’t. Booker never attempted to go on a superstar surge to get back into the ballgame. item.title: WNBA Fans Might Not Be Ready for This Angel Reese Take
item.description: Aug 30, 2026; College Park, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) reacts with teammates during the game against the Minnesota Lynx at Gateway Center Arena at College Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images IS ANGEL REESE ONE OF THE MOST OVERRATED PLAYERS IN THE WNBA? Before the comments explode, let’s have an honest conversation. Angel Reese is one of the biggest names in women’s basketball. She gets attention, drives engagement and has one of the most passionate fan bases in the sport. But are we talking enough about what happens between the lines? Reese scored just seven points in Atlanta’s 64-55 loss to Golden State on Monday night. The Dream now trail 3-2 in the WNBA Finals, and their season is hanging by a thread. Her supporters will point to her rebounding, physicality and the impact she has beyond scoring. Fair enough. Those things matter. But the biggest stars are judged by what they deliver when the pressure is highest. And when the offense is struggling, a player with Reese’s profile has to find ways to make a bigger impact. The uncomfortable question is whether the hype surrounding Reese has outpaced her offensive development. That doesn’t mean she isn’t talented. It doesn’t mean she can’t improve. And it certainly doesn’t mean one bad game defines her career. But if we can’t question a star after a performance like that, what exactly are we allowed to criticize? BE HONEST: Is Angel Reese underrated because people focus on the hate, or overrated because the hype has gotten too big? No fence-sitting. We want to hear your argument.

item.title: Major Franz Wagner Trade Package Pitched For Brooklyn Nets
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 25: Franz Wagner #22 of the Orlando Magic holds the ball during the first quarter of the game against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on October 25, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) Getty The Brooklyn Nets and Orlando Magic are both in difficult situations early into the NBA season. Brooklyn is currently 0-3 and doesn’t own their own draft pick this season to make the losing even more heartbreaking for the fan base. Orlando is limiting expectations after Paolo Banchero suffered an injury to miss at least one month of action. A trade was pitched that could help both teams moving forward. Bleacher Report’s trade expert Zach Buckley predicted a realistic trade package that would land the Nets Franz Wagner: “Orlando Magic receive: Michael Porter Jr., 2027 first-round pick (via NYK), 2028 first-round pick (1-8 protected, via PHI), 2029 second-round pick (via GSW) and 2029 second-round pick (via MEM) Brooklyn Nets receive: Franz Wagner” The trade would see Brooklyn giving up two first round picks, multiple second round picks and Porter to the Magic. Franz’s brother Mo Wagner currently plays for the Nets and has loved living in Brooklyn for years now. The family ties could present Franz with an ideal location for personal happiness and to have more control on a rebuilding team. Nets management making such a trade would see Wagner becoming the new face of the franchise with fellow young stars Egor Demin and Mikel Brown behind him. Why Orlando Would Trade Franz Wagner Orlando has run into the same issues every season with both Wagner and Banchero failing to play effectively together. This season started off 0-2 before Banchero got injured. Wagner led the Magic to a shocking upset victory over the New York Knicks in Madison Square Garden. Banchero missing more time means that Orlando will have another start to the season unsure of whether their two stars can play together. The Magic invested a lot in Desmond Bane via draft picks and an expensive contract extension to be the third star to Banchero and Wagner. However, the process continues to see the same issue playing out. Banchero is considered more valuable than Wagner since he’s a former number one pick with more obvious talent. Trading Franz to Brooklyn would give them a strong starter in Porter and draft picks back for the future. Porter has shown he can average 20+ points for the Nets and has contributed to title contention with the Denver Nuggets in the past. Nets Badly Need Franz Wagner Or Similar Player Brooklyn traded for Julius Randle to add more talent to the roster and hopefully win enough games to avoid losing a high draft pick. Randle and Porter have both played well for the Nets, but it has not led to any impact on winning. A 0-3 star

item.title: Chicago Bulls coach Thiago Splitter on facing Boston Celtics 3-point barrage
item.description: The Boston Celtics beat the Chicago Bulls with a barrage of shots from beyond the arc (including a huge third quarter from deep from Payton Pritchard), the sort of outcome fans of the storied ball club know well. But it was the first time at the helm of his own team that new Chicago Bulls head coach Thiago Splitter faced such a barrage from Boston in that role. Not, however, that it surprised him, even so. "Well, I mean, this is their game, right? They’re going to shoot 50 3s a game, and they have good shooters," said Splitter. "You have to be able to guard them. I think Pritchard had a great game. Pull up 3s one on one against different players. Yes, we could have like blitzed him or doubled him, but you know they also create rotations and you have catch and shoot 3s, so it’s not that easy. You know they do a good job." "They play with what they got, and you know the biggest reason is you have got to rebound the ball better," he added. "We have got to take care of the ball, and shoot better on offense as well." "They literally grab every offensive rebound," continued the Bulls coach. "They made 3s, contested 3s. I mean, we knew that they are a very good team shooting a 3-ball, but when you give them second and third chances, it’s impossible." "And you have got to get better. I mean, those third quarters were very bad to say the least. And we have got to fix it mentally. Whatever it is, we have got to start those third quarters better." Listen to "What went wrong in the Celtics Opening Night loss to the Pistons" on Spreaker. item.title: Nuggets’ Aaron Gordon gets ejected from Warriors clash after double technical fouls
item.description: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Nuggets’ Aaron Gordon gets ejected from Warriors clash after double technical fouls appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Nuggets lost the plot in the second half of an eventual 134-114 loss against the Golden State Warriors, and no other play encapsulated that better than Aaron Gordon racking up two technical fouls in quick succession. With the Warriors leading by 16 points, 107-91, the Nuggets knew that every possession matters from that point forward. Alas, they would turn the ball over, with Christian Braun being whistled for a push off on Stephen Curry. This infuriated Gordon beyond belief. He made the officials know that he did not agree with the foul they called on Braun, and the Nuggets forward vehemently protested, incurring a technical foul. Not even close to being done, Gordon then pointed towards an official as a way of expressing his frustrations. This would then net him his second technical, ending his night prematurely in a matter of seconds with an ejection. Aaron Gordon gets hit with two quick technical fouls, each from every ref, and is ejected from the game, with 8:37 minutes remaining in the 4th quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Including Curry's bucket – 8/8 from the field pic.twitter.com/Ok6W6wAzGA — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 27, 2026 Gordon was already having a rough outing prior to getting himself ejected. In just 25 minutes of play, the Nuggets forward put up just seven points on 2-of-10 shooting from the field. Considering how the Nuggets’ depth isn’t the best to begin with, losing Gordon just proved to be the nail in the coffin of a disastrous night for Denver. The Nuggets were already without Cameron Johnson and Julian Strawther heading into the night, so Gordon was expected to take on a bigger scoring role to lighten Nikola Jokic and Murray’s burden. Alas, Gordon simply has not shot the ball well over the past two games, combining to shoot 4-of-18 during that span. There is legitimate concern regarding the Nuggets’ contending viability moving forward. Their offense is sputtering, their defense is all out of sorts, and nights like this from Gordon aren’t going to help whatsoever. The fact that the Nuggets had to overturn a 23-point deficit to earn their first win back on Saturday is a red flag as well. Nonetheless, it is still early in the season, and the Nuggets will look to earn their second win of the campaign when they take on the Pelicans on Wednesday night. Related: DeMar DeRozan’s post about ‘darkness’ has fans concerned Related: Warriors vs. Nuggets injury report: Cam Johnson set to miss another game

item.title: Angel Reese Needs Help, But Is She the Problem, Too?
item.description: Sep 30, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) flashes a sign to an ESPN camera after game two of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs against the Washington Mystics at CareFirst Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rafael Suanes-Imagn Images ANGEL REESE CAN’T CARRY THE ATLANTA DREAM. BUT IS SHE HELPING ENOUGH? 🔥 Let’s make one thing clear: Atlanta’s offensive problems are bigger than one player. The Dream scored just 55 points in Monday night’s 64-55 loss to the Golden State Valkyries. Now, Atlanta trails 3-2 in the WNBA Finals and faces a must-win situation. Reese scored seven points. Her supporters will point out that Golden State has made scoring in the paint difficult and that Atlanta needs more production from the rest of its roster. That’s a legitimate argument. But critics have a point, too. Reese previously showed her ceiling with a 30-point, 16-rebound performance in Game 2. That is the version of Reese Atlanta needs if it hopes to survive. The question isn’t whether Reese is talented. It’s whether she can consistently deliver offensively against the best competition when the pressure rises. If the Dream lose this series, the blame shouldn’t automatically fall entirely on Reese. But she shouldn’t be completely exempt from criticism, either. Pick a side: 🔥 TEAM ANGEL: Atlanta’s supporting cast is letting her down. 👀 TEAM CRITICS: Reese has to be better when it matters most. Who is right? Don’t just vote — explain why in the comments.

item.title: Oregon’s Dan Lanning Announces Devastating News on QB Dante Moore
item.description: EUGENE, OREGON - SEPTEMBER 5: Quarterback Dante Moore #5 of the Oregon Ducks looks up at the scoreboard during the second half of the game against the Boise State Broncos at Autzen Stadium on September 5, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) Getty It’s been a nightmare of a 2026 season for the Oregon Ducks, who entered the year as the No. 2-ranked team in the AP Poll. Fast-forward to the final week of October, and they’re coming off their third loss of the season to the Illinois Fighting Illini and are now unranked. While their struggles began early with a loss to Oklahoma State, things only got worse when star quarterback and expected first-round pick Dante Moore suffered a scary concussion against the USC Trojans that forced him to leave the game on a stretcher and in an ambulance. Fortunately, doctors cleared Moore after his concussion. Although the injury has kept him sidelined for the last few weeks, he has continued traveling with the team and supporting his teammates from the sidelines. Dan Lanning Announces Devastating News on Moore After their latest loss, which likely killed their College Football Playoff hopes, Oregon head coach Dan Lanning announced a devastating update on Moore’s status as fans held out hope that he’d return at some point this season. However, that won’t be the case. Lanning revealed Monday evening that Moore isn’t expected to play again this season for the Ducks. That would end his college career with his final snaps coming in that USC game as a member of Oregon’s football program. NEW: Oregon star QB Dante Moore is not expected to return this season due to injury, Dan Lanning announced. https://t.co/nSQNJM6ZS7 — On3 (@On3) October 27, 2026 Lanning’s Previous Comments on Moore Earlier this month, when it seemed Oregon still had everything in front of them, Lanning sounded optimistic when asked whether Moore would return. “Dante was out there at practice for us today,” Lanning said earlier this month. “Similar to what we’ve said before, we’re gonna continue to make sure we do what’s best for Dante as we move forward. Obviously, we’ll have an injury report released later on this week that will detail what that looks like. But it was great to see him back out there with his teammates able to get a little work in today.” Ultimately, what’s best for Moore is focusing on the next phase of his football career at the NFL level rather than risking another injury or jeopardizing his chances of reaching the pros. Oregon appears to be out of contention at this point, making a return even less worthwhile. With Moore now expected to miss the rest of the season, Dylan Raiola will continue as the starter, with Brock Thomas serving as the backup. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Oregon’s Dan Lanning Announces Devastating News on QB Dante Moore appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Rockets’ Alperen Sengun joins Nikola Jokic in rare club with eye-popping stats vs. Hawks
item.description: Credit: Erik Williams-Imagn Images Rockets’ Alperen Sengun joins Nikola Jokic in rare club with eye-popping stats vs. Hawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Rockets have looked like one of the best teams in the NBA through the first few games of the 2026-27 season. Their hot start to the new campaign continued on Monday, as they rode a strong night from Alperen Sengun to defeat the Atlanta Hawks for the second straight time, taking a 120-110 victory at home. Sengun had his way with the Hawks’ overmatched frontline. He put up 29 points, nine rebounds, and nine assists, and he also was his peak disruptive self on defense, adding six thefts as well to what was already such a stacked stat line. By putting up that kind of performance in the Rockets’ latest win, he joined Nikola Jokic as the only centers in NBA history to reach those numbers in a single game, according to StatMuse on X. It sure looks like playing alongside a legitimate floor general in Fred VanVleet is making Sengun’s life easier. He can catch the ball along the high post instead of having to go through hoops just to get the ball in good post position, and the burden to organize the offense no longer falls solely on his shoulders. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It’s not a coincidence at all that Sengun’s biggest scoring performances of the season have come with VanVleet on the active roster. When VanVleet was out due to load management during their first matchup against the Hawks back on Saturday, Sengun scored just 17 points — his lowest tally of the season thus far. Everything is humming for the Rockets at the moment, and the clean bill of health for most of the team’s core players is enabling this level of play from Sengun. On the season, he is averaging 24.5 points, 9.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists, and 1.8 steals on 58/66/77 shooting splits. The Rockets will look to make it five wins in a row on Wednesday when they take on the Milwaukee Bucks on the road at 8:00 PM E.T. Related: Hawks vs. Rockets injury report: Marcus Smart listed in rematch showdown Related: Rockets’ Alperen Sengun rattles the rim with insane slam dunk vs. Hawks

item.title: Prescott lifts Dallas Cowboys to 38-21 win over Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A general view of the NFL logo prior to the start of match 10 of the main round of the NFL American football match between Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Seattle Seahawks at the Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Prescott lifts Dallas Cowboys to 38-21 win over Philadelphia Eagles») Sven Hoppe/dpa A dominant performance from quarterback Dak Prescott led the Dallas Cowboys to a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Prescott threw for three touchdowns and 212 yards without a turnover as Dallas found the end zone in each quarter. The Eagles stayed within touching distance of the Cowboys until the final period, but were unable to find a response to Javonte Williams' two-yard rushing touchdown with 2:21 left on the clock. Philadelphia's back-up quarterback Tanner McKee finished with a touchdown and one interception in the loss.

Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. It is some effort for his job to be so under threat when only Arsenal (57 points) and Manchester City (56) have been more productive than United (46) during the 45-year-old’s tenure. The tally obscures pertinent facts. United topping the Premier League during his 17‑match interim spell last season is irrelevant when they sit 16th with no win in eight games in all competitions this season. Losing narrowly against City is one thing, but three-goal defeats by Como and Bournemouth will surely spell managerial change. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net. Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Osula and Barnes strike as Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace
item.description: The first half was dreadful. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit. Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure . Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...
